literature.headline_zh: 麻疹病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期麻疹病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 审查得出的结论是,MMR 疫苗 仍然是暴露 72 小时内 麻疹 PEP 的一线干预措施,IG 保留用于 疫苗接种 禁忌或可能无效的情况。由于许多临床医生和公共卫生专业人员的第一手 麻疹 经验有限,它强调了临床指导的必要性。 [10.1093/ajhp/zxag315]
MeV RT-PCR 检测的检测限为每毫升 500 个 基因组 拷贝。该测定针对 85 个不同的样品进行了测试:50 个阳性临床样品和参考材料以及 35 个阴性临床样品或参考材料。该测定显示 100% 测定间和测定内重现性。 [10.1093/labmed/lmag075]
在所有报告的指标系列中,选择滞后关联均为负值,领先时间为 1-9 周。Cq 和 DGE 衍生的 R t 之间最强的负相关发生在第二次吉娃娃波的 +8 周(r = -0.745)和哈利斯科州的 +7 周(r = -0.464)。只有哈利斯科州支持完全调整的型号 4 (M4)。 [10.3389/fpubh.2026.1967103]
在 PM 中,我们发现 麻疹病毒 (MV) 的溶瘤活性主要依赖于 I 型干扰素 (IFN-I) 途径的改变。我们首先证明了 VMOC 具有适当的内皮屏障完整性、可灌注性和血管对外部刺激的反应性的功能。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11276689/v1]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Among 804 children, case status was associated with non-vaccination (aOR 2.12, 95% CI 1.02–4.42), close contact (3.00, 1.72–5.25), reported health-facility attendance (2.79, 1.91–4.06), vaccine unavailability (2.62, 1.17–5.85), and trucked/vendor water (2.98, 2.03–4.36). [10.1093/inthealth/ihag102]

The review concludes that the MMR vaccine remains the first-line intervention for measles PEP within 72 hours of exposure, with IG reserved for cases where vaccination is contraindicated or potentially ineffective. [10.1093/ajhp/zxag315]

The MeV RT-PCR assay has a limit of detection of 500 genome copies per milliliter. The assay was tested against 85 different samples: 50 positive clinical samples and reference materials and 35 negative clinical samples or reference materials. The assay showed 100% interassay and intra-assay reproducibility. [10.1093/labmed/lmag075]

Selected-lag associations were negative across all reported metric families, at leads of 1–9 weeks. The strongest negative correlation between Cq and DGE-derived R t occurred at +8 weeks in the second Chihuahua wave ( r = −0.745) and at +7 weeks in Jalisco ( r = −0.464). [10.3389/fpubh.2026.1967103]

A total of 7,149 measles cases were included. The overall incidence of measles was 33.28 per 100,000 inhabitants. Males were overrepresented, accounting for 51.45% of cases. news.headline_zh: 美洲宗教集会前麻疹传播风险被泛美卫生组织评估为非常高。
news.lead_zh: 泛美卫生组织 (PAHO) 发布区域风险评估,指出美洲地区麻疹传播风险非常高,尤其在宗教群众集会前。
key_findings_zh: PAHO 指出 2026 年 1 月 4 日至 10 月 3 日,17 个国家和地区报告了 55,792 例确诊病例。
PAHO 强调需要加强疫苗接种、监测和快速反应措施以减少麻疹传播风险。

PAHO 正在通过技术合作、实验室监测和基因组监测来支持各国应对麻疹。

news.trend_or_risk_zh: 麻疹传播风险显著上升,尤其在美洲地区,与宗教集会相关。
news.caveats_zh: 部分数据可能未完全更新,具体传播路径尚待进一步确认。
news.headline_en: PAHO assesses very high risk of measles spread ahead of religious mass gatherings in the Americas.
news.lead_en: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has issued a regional risk assessment indicating a very high risk of measles spread in the Americas ahead of upcoming religious mass gatherings.
key_findings_en: PAHO reported 55,792 confirmed measles cases and 77 deaths in 17 countries and territories from January 4 to October 3, 2026.
Guatemala, Mexico, the United States, Peru, and Canada accounted for 99.5% of the cases.
Religious mass gatherings are expected to increase travel and population movement, creating more opportunities for the virus to spread.
PAHO is supporting countries with technical cooperation, laboratory-based surveillance, and genomic monitoring to enhance outbreak response.
The warning highlights the consequences of vaccination gaps and the potential for imported cases through international travel.
news.trend_or_risk_en: Measles transmission risk is rising, especially in the Americas, linked to religious gatherings.
news.caveats_en: Some data may not be fully updated, and specific transmission pathways remain to be confirmed.
news.brief_en: PAHO has issued a regional risk assessment indicating a very high risk of measles spread in the Americas ahead of upcoming religious mass gatherings. These gatherings are expected to increase travel and population movement, creating more opportunities for the virus to spread. The assessment notes that between 4 January and 3 October 2026, 55,792 confirmed measles cases and 77 deaths were reported in 17 countries and territories, marking a 4.8-fold increase compared to the same period in 2025. PAHO emphasizes the need for stronger vaccination coverage, surveillance, and rapid response measures to mitigate the risk. The organization is supporting countries with technical cooperation, laboratory-based surveillance, and genomic monitoring to enhance preparedness and response capabilities. The warning underscores the consequences of vaccination gaps and the potential for imported cases through international travel, particularly in communities with low immunity.

papers.title: Immunoglobulin Use, Availability, and Administration Considerations in Measles Prevention
papers.abstract: Abstract In 2026, the National Foundation for Infectious Diseases (NFID), with the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), convened a Measles Summit in response to the largest U.S. measles resurgence in over three decades, with more than 3,000 confirmed cases mostly among unvaccinated individuals. Many clinicians and public health professionals have limited firsthand measles experience, underscoring the need for clinical guidance. In this commentary, we examine immune globulin (IG) use for measles post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) amid fragile supply and logistical challenges. GamaSTAN®, the sole Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-licensed intramuscular IG product, faces episodic availability, non-returnable single-vial economics, and a 2013 recommendation to double the PEP dose, increasing per-patient demand. IVIG is increasingly employed when patients weigh 30 kg or more, beyond the weight at which an adequate dose of immune globulin can be given intramuscularly, or when IMIG supply is constrained, while concurrent lot withdrawals compromise institutional formularies. We review evidence-based patient selection for PEP, emphasizing that the Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) vaccine remains first-line within 72 hours of exposure, with IG reserved when vaccination is contraindicated or potentially ineffective. Immunosuppressive therapies vary widely in their effects on the safety and efficacy of live vaccines. We therefore argue against categorizing every biologic, immunomodulator, or steroid as an automatic MMR contraindication, which would overestimate IG-PEP demand and preclude MMR for eligible patients. We propose class-specific stratification and an electronic health record decision-support rule to better align IG demand with genuine need. Finally, we address declining potency standards for measles antibody, attributable to waning donor titers, and offer guidance on dosing, multi-site pediatric administration, and infusion logistics within the PEP window.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on measles virus, specifically examining the use, availability, and administration considerations of immune globulin (IG) for post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) against measles. The central question is how to optimize IG use in measles prevention, particularly in the context of supply constraints and logistical challenges.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a commentary, not a systematic review or meta-analysis. It discusses the context of the measles resurgence in the U.S. and the challenges surrounding IG supply, including the FDA-licensed GamaSTAN® product's single-vial economics and the 2013 recommendation to double the PEP dose. It also highlights the increasing use of IVIG in certain patient populations due to IMIG limitations.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the MMR vaccine remains the first-line intervention for measles PEP within 72 hours of exposure, with IG reserved for cases where vaccination is contraindicated or potentially ineffective. It emphasizes the need for clinical guidance due to limited firsthand measles experience among many clinicians and public health professionals.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that immunosuppressive therapies vary in their effects on the safety and efficacy of live vaccines, and it argues against categorizing all biologics, immunomodulators, or steroids as automatic MMR contraindications. It also highlights the declining potency of measles antibodies due to waning donor titers, which may affect dosing and administration strategies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes class-specific stratification of patients for IG use and suggests implementing an electronic health record decision-support rule to better align IG demand with genuine need. It also calls for guidance on dosing, multi-site pediatric administration, and infusion logistics within the PEP window.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses the use of immune globulin (IG) for measles post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) amid supply and logistical challenges. It highlights the resurgence of measles in the U.S. and the limitations of the FDA-licensed GamaSTAN® product, including its single-vial economics and the 2013 recommendation to double the PEP dose. The review emphasizes that the MMR vaccine remains the first-line intervention for measles PEP within 72 hours of exposure, with IG reserved for cases where vaccination is contraindicated or ineffective. It also discusses the variability of immunosuppressive therapies' effects on live vaccines and the declining potency of measles antibodies due to waning donor titers. The authors propose class-specific stratification and electronic health record decision-support rules to better align IG demand with actual need, while also addressing dosing and administration challenges within the PEP window.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on measles virus, specifically examining the use, availability, and administration considerations of immune globulin (IG) for post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) against measles. The central question is how to optimize IG use in measles prevention, particularly in the context of supply constraints and logistical challenges.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a commentary, not a systematic review or meta-analysis. It discusses the context of the measles resurgence in the U.S. and the challenges surrounding IG supply, including the FDA-licensed GamaSTAN® product's single-vial economics and the 2013 recommendation to double the PEP dose. It also highlights the increasing use of IVIG in certain patient populations due to IMIG limitations.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the MMR vaccine remains the first-line intervention for measles PEP within 72 hours of exposure, with IG reserved for cases where vaccination is contraindicated or potentially ineffective. It emphasizes the need for clinical guidance due to limited firsthand measles experience among many clinicians and public health professionals.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that immunosuppressive therapies vary in their effects on the safety and efficacy of live vaccines, and it argues against categorizing all biologics, immunomodulators, or steroids as automatic MMR contraindications. It also highlights the declining potency of measles antibodies due to waning donor titers, which may affect dosing and administration strategies.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes class-specific stratification of patients for IG use and suggests implementing an electronic health record decision-support rule to better align IG demand with genuine need. It also calls for guidance on dosing, multi-site pediatric administration, and infusion logistics within the PEP window.

papers.title_zh: 麻疹 预防中免疫球蛋白的使用、可用性和给药注意事项
papers.source_body_en: Abstract In 2026, the National Foundation for Infectious Diseases (NFID), with the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), convened a Measles Summit in response to the largest U.S. measles resurgence in over three decades, with more than 3,000 confirmed cases mostly among unvaccinated individuals. Many clinicians and public health professionals have limited firsthand measles experience, underscoring the need for clinical guidance. In this commentary, we examine immune globulin (IG) use for measles post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) amid fragile supply and logistical challenges. GamaSTAN®, the sole Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-licensed intramuscular IG product, faces episodic availability, non-returnable single-vial economics, and a 2013 recommendation to double the PEP dose, increasing per-patient demand. IVIG is increasingly employed when patients weigh 30 kg or more, beyond the weight at which an adequate dose of immune globulin can be given intramuscularly, or when IMIG supply is constrained, while concurrent lot withdrawals compromise institutional formularies. We review evidence-based patient selection for PEP, emphasizing that the Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) vaccine remains first-line within 72 hours of exposure, with IG reserved when vaccination is contraindicated or potentially ineffective. Immunosuppressive therapies vary widely in their effects on the safety and efficacy of live vaccines. We therefore argue against categorizing every biologic, immunomodulator, or steroid as an automatic MMR contraindication, which would overestimate IG-PEP demand and preclude MMR for eligible patients. We propose class-specific stratification and an electronic health record decision-support rule to better align IG demand with genuine need. Finally, we address declining potency standards for measles antibody, attributable to waning donor titers, and offer guidance on dosing, multi-site pediatric administration, and infusion logistics within the PEP window.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 2026年,美国国家传染病基金会(NFID)与美国传染病学会(IDSA)召开了麻疹峰会,以应对美国三十多年来最大规模的麻疹疫情卷土重来,确诊病例超过3000例,其中大部分是未接种疫苗的个体。许多临床医生和公共卫生专业人员的第一手 麻疹 经验有限,这强调了临床指导的必要性。在这篇评论中,我们研究了在供应脆弱和后勤挑战的情况下免疫球蛋白 (IG) 在 麻疹 暴露后预防 (PEP) 中的使用。GamaSTAN® 是唯一获得美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 许可的肌内 IG 产品,面临着间歇性供应、不可回收的单瓶经济问题,以及 2013 年建议将 PEP 剂量加倍,从而增加了每位患者的需求。当患者体重超过 30 公斤或以上,超过可以肌内注射足够剂量的免疫球蛋白的体重时,或者当 IMIG 供应受到限制时,IVIG 的使用越来越多,同时批次撤回会损害机构处方。我们回顾了 PEP 的基于证据的患者选择,强调 麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗 在暴露后 72 小时内仍然是一线药物,当 疫苗接种 有禁忌或可能无效时,保留 IG。免疫抑制疗法对活体 疫苗 安全性和有效性的影响差异很大。因此,我们反对将每种生物制剂、免疫调节剂或类固醇归类为自动 MMR 禁忌症,这会高估 IG-PEP 需求并排除符合条件的患者的 MMR。我们提出针对特定类别的分层和电子健康记录决策支持规则,以更好地将 IG 需求与真实需求保持一致。最后,我们解决了由于供体滴度下降而导致的 麻疹 抗体效力标准下降的问题,并提供了 PEP 窗口内的剂量、多部位儿科给药和输注物流方面的指导。

papers.title: Efficient host transmission of measles virus: disentangling misconceptions from established findings
papers.abstract: SUMMARY Measles virus (MeV) is considered the most contagious human virus. This review critically examines explanations for MeV’s extraordinary transmissibility. Although substantial progress has been made in understanding MeV infection, pathogenesis, and host spread, the fundamental question of why MeV is markedly more transmissible than other structurally similar respiratory viruses within the same taxonomic families remains unresolved. Many commonly cited explanations are either incorrect, oversimplified, or insufficiently supported by rigorous experimental evidence. Notably, there is a striking lack of studies that directly investigate the mechanisms governing MeV transmission. This knowledge gap persists in part because humans are the only natural reservoir for MeV, and thus the most relevant experimental models can be costly, technically challenging, and limited in ability. Moreover, studies addressing MeV environmental stability have relied largely on in vitro laboratory conditions that may have limited relevance to real-world transmission scenarios. While these studies have yielded useful observations, they often lack definitive mechanistic insight into efficient host-to-host spread. In this review, we discuss multiple strategies to investigate and define the efficient transmission of MeV, including (i) epidemiology, (ii) stability in controlled environments, (iii) infectious dose, (iv) incubation period, and (v) shedding from the respiratory epithelium. As will be discussed, quantitative, head-to-head comparisons of MeV transmission dynamics with those of other common respiratory viruses, such as influenza virus, rhinovirus, and respiratory syncytial virus, are notably absent. A clearer understanding of the mechanisms that govern efficient MeV transmission may inform strategies to reduce spread in educational, healthcare, and community settings.

papers.title: The 2026 measles resurgence in Bangladesh and its public health implications
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Measles has resurged globally in the post-pandemic period as routine immunisation recovery remains below the two-dose threshold required to interrupt transmission. Bangladesh, previously nearing measles–rubella elimination, entered 2026 with widening coverage gaps, depleted vaccine stocks, and increasing numbers of missed children. We conducted a situation analysis to assess the scale, concentration, and programmatic implications of the outbreak. Methods We performed a rapid mixed-evidence review from 11–15 April 2026 using data from WHO, UNICEF, DGHS bulletins, PubMed/MEDLINE, ReliefWeb, SEARO updates, and Bangla-language media. Of 46 records screened, 19 were included. Analysis was based on aggregated, publicly available surveillance and programme data. Findings The DGHS measles press release dated 15 April 2026 reported cumulative totals since 15 March of 19,161 suspected cases, 2,973 confirmed cases, 166 suspected deaths, and 32 confirmed deaths; a WHO update dated 15 April reported 58 affected districts. The cumulative suspected-case burden was spatially concentrated: Dhaka and Rajshahi together accounted for 62.7% of suspected cases, and the division-level HHI was 0.255. Children under five comprised 81% of cases, including 34% infants under nine months. Vaccination status showed 72% zero-dose and 16% partially vaccinated cases. Valid MR1 coverage declined from 88.6% in 2019 to 86.1% in 2023, while valid MR2 coverage declined from 89.1% to 80.7%, indicating a widening immunity gap. Interpretation The resurgence reflects accumulated immunity gaps rather than vaccine failure, driven by subnational inequities and programme disruption. Urgent priorities include targeted vaccination campaigns, restoration of vitamin A supplementation, strengthening paediatric care capacity, and integrating real-time surveillance into outbreak response.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Measles has resurged globally in the post-pandemic period as routine immunisation recovery remains below the two-dose threshold required to interrupt transmission. Methods We performed a rapid mixed-evidence review from 11–15 April 2026 using data from WHO, UNICEF, DGHS bulletins, PubMed/MEDLINE, ReliefWeb, SEARO updates, and Bangla-language media. papers.title: Factors associated with measles infection during the 2025–6 outbreak in Burao, Somaliland: a case-control study
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives Somaliland has recurrent measles transmission, but outbreak-specific evidence on modifiable child, household, and health-service factors is limited. We examined factors associated with measles case status during the 2025–6 Burao outbreak. Methods We conducted a community-based unmatched case-control study among children aged <15 years from 14 June to 8 July 2026. Cases were enrolled consecutively and controls sampled systematically from households using a random start and every fourth household. Cluster-robust logistic regression estimated adjusted ORs (aORs), with indeterminate responses modeled separately. Results Among 804 children (290 cases, 514 controls), case status was associated with non-vaccination (aOR 2.12, 95% CI 1.02–4.42), close contact (3.00, 1.72–5.25), reported health-facility attendance (2.79, 1.91–4.06), vaccine unavailability (2.62, 1.17–5.85), and trucked/vendor water (2.98, 2.03–4.36). Prior malnutrition, large-gathering attendance, household vaccination-refusal history, and poor ventilation were also associated. Health-facility attendance referred to the 21 days before rash onset/reference date, but exact visit dates were not collected. Conclusion Measles case status was associated with immunity gaps, contact, household conditions, and service-related factors. Response priorities include reliable vaccine availability, catch-up vaccination, and contact-based action. The health-facility attendance association is temporally ambiguous and does not establish healthcare-associated transmission.

Response priorities include reliable vaccine availability, catch-up vaccination, and contact-based action. The health-facility attendance association is temporally ambiguous and does not establish healthcare-associated transmission.

analysis.summary_en: This case-control study investigated factors associated with measles infection during the 2025–6 outbreak in Burao, Somaliland. The research aimed to address the lack of outbreak-specific evidence on modifiable factors influencing measles transmission. Among 804 children, non-vaccination, close contact, health-facility attendance, vaccine unavailability, and use of trucked/vendor water were significantly associated with measles case status. The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting immunity gaps, contact patterns, household conditions, and service-related factors contributing to the outbreak. The study's results suggest that improving vaccine availability, promoting catch-up vaccination, and implementing contact-based prevention strategies could be critical for controlling measles. However, the temporally ambiguous health-facility attendance association and the case-control design limit the confidence in the causal interpretations. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

papers.title: Population-level measles RT–PCR cycle threshold values and their relationships with disease severity, transmission, and incidence metrics: a time series analysis of the 2025–2026 outbreak in Mexico
papers.abstract: Objectives To determine whether the weekly median real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT–PCR) quantification cycle (Cq) value of notified measles cases precedes the incidence, transmission, and severity metrics of an outbreak. We focused particularly on the effective reproduction number ( R t ). We also assessed whether any association persisted after adjustment for a linear time trend, specimen composition, and the outcome's own past. Methods We conducted a retrospective secondary analysis of 10,910 Cq determinations and 11,735 confirmed cases recorded in a single Mexican national case-level surveillance extract for Chihuahua and Jalisco. Twelve reported weekly metrics of incidence, transmission, and severity were examined by cross-correlation, four nested lagged regression models (M1–M4), formal Toda–Yamamoto Granger tests, and a secondary calibrated-lag autoregressive model. Moving-block bootstrap intervals were the primary method for regression inference. Autocorrelation-robust and classical methods were used in sensitivity analyses. Individual Cq determinations were analyzed separately against collection timing, severity, and vaccination history. Results Selected-lag associations were negative across all reported metric families, at leads of 1–9 weeks. The strongest negative correlation between Cq and DGE-derived R t occurred at +8 weeks in the second Chihuahua wave ( r = −0.745). In Jalisco, it occurred at +7 weeks ( r = −0.464). Only Jalisco supported the fully adjusted model 4 (M4). There, bootstrap intervals excluded zero for both the laboratory-positive-case and final surveillance-confirmed-case R t estimates but not for the two severity proportions. Excluding up to four endpoint weeks preserved the direction of both R t estimates. At the individual level, Cq increased with zero, one, and two documented vaccine doses (0.761 cycles per dose, 95% CI 0.589 to 0.932) and was 1.02 cycles lower in hospitalized cases. Conclusions Aggregate Cq showed the most consistent retrospective leading association with R t . The retrospective associations occurred at data-calibrated lags of 7–8 weeks during the second Chihuahua wave and in Jalisco. Conversely, leak-free forecasting supported incremental gain in one analytic unit at a median 2-week horizon. The operational predictive horizon of aggregate Cq therefore remains unvalidated. If prospectively validated, weekly aggregate Cq could complement conventional measles surveillance using laboratory information that is already routinely collected.

papers.title_zh: 人群水平 麻疹 RT-PCR 循环阈值及其与疾病严重程度、传播 和 发病率 指标的关系:墨西哥 2025-2026 年 暴发 的时间序列分析
papers.source_body_en: Objectives To determine whether the weekly median real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT–PCR) quantification cycle (Cq) value of notified measles cases precedes the incidence, transmission, and severity metrics of an outbreak. We focused particularly on the effective reproduction number ( R t ). We also assessed whether any association persisted after adjustment for a linear time trend, specimen composition, and the outcome's own past. Methods We conducted a retrospective secondary analysis of 10,910 Cq determinations and 11,735 confirmed cases recorded in a single Mexican national case-level surveillance extract for Chihuahua and Jalisco. Twelve reported weekly metrics of incidence, transmission, and severity were examined by cross-correlation, four nested lagged regression models (M1–M4), formal Toda–Yamamoto Granger tests, and a secondary calibrated-lag autoregressive model. Moving-block bootstrap intervals were the primary method for regression inference. Autocorrelation-robust and classical methods were used in sensitivity analyses. Individual Cq determinations were analyzed separately against collection timing, severity, and vaccination history. Results Selected-lag associations were negative across all reported metric families, at leads of 1–9 weeks. The strongest negative correlation between Cq and DGE-derived R t occurred at +8 weeks in the second Chihuahua wave ( r = −0.745). In Jalisco, it occurred at +7 weeks ( r = −0.464). Only Jalisco supported the fully adjusted model 4 (M4). There, bootstrap intervals excluded zero for both the laboratory-positive-case and final surveillance-confirmed-case R t estimates but not for the two severity proportions. Excluding up to four endpoint weeks preserved the direction of both R t estimates. At the individual level, Cq increased with zero, one, and two documented vaccine doses (0.761 cycles per dose, 95% CI 0.589 to 0.932) and was 1.02 cycles lower in hospitalized cases. Conclusions Aggregate Cq showed the most consistent retrospective leading association with R t . The retrospective associations occurred at data-calibrated lags of 7–8 weeks during the second Chihuahua wave and in Jalisco. Conversely, leak-free forecasting supported incremental gain in one analytic unit at a median 2-week horizon. The operational predictive horizon of aggregate Cq therefore remains unvalidated. If prospectively validated, weekly aggregate Cq could complement conventional measles surveillance using laboratory information that is already routinely collected.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的 确定通知的麻疹病例的每周中位数实时逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT–PCR)定量循环(Cq)值是否在发病率、传播和严重程度指标之前发生。我们特别关注有效繁殖数(Rt)。我们还评估了在调整线性时间趋势、样本组成和结果自身历史后,任何关联是否仍然存在。方法 我们对墨西哥一个国家层面的监测数据集进行了回顾性二次分析,该数据集记录了奇瓦瓦州和哈利斯科州的10,910个Cq测定值和11,735个确诊病例。通过交叉相关分析、四个嵌套滞后回归模型(M1–M4)、正式的Toda–Yamamoto格兰杰检验以及一个二次校准滞后自回归模型,分析了十二周报告的发病率、传播和严重程度指标。移动块自举区间是回归推断的主要方法。在敏感性分析中使用了自相关稳健和经典方法。对个体Cq测定值分别与采集时间、严重程度和疫苗接种历史进行分析。结果 所选滞后关联在所有报告的指标家族中均为负值,滞后时间为1至9周。在奇瓦瓦州第二波中,Cq与DGE衍生的Rt之间的最强负相关出现在+8周(r = −0.745)。在哈利斯科州,出现在+7周(r = −0.464)。只有哈利斯科州支持完全调整的模型4(M4)。在那里,自举区间排除了零,对于实验室阳性病例和最终监测确认病例的Rt估计值,但未排除两个严重程度比例。排除最多四个终点周仍保留了两个Rt估计值的方向。在个体层面,Cq随着零、一、两剂记录的疫苗剂量而增加(每剂0.761个循环,95% CI 0.589至0.932),并且住院病例的Cq值比非住院病例低1.02个循环。结论 整体Cq在回顾性分析中与Rt表现出最一致的领先关联。回顾性关联发生在奇瓦瓦州第二波和哈利斯科州的数据校准滞后7–8周。相反,无泄漏的预测支持在一个分析单位中,中位数2周的预测范围内有逐步增加。因此,整体Cq的操作性预测范围尚未验证。如果前瞻性验证成功,每周整体Cq可能可以补充传统的麻疹监测,利用已经常规收集的实验室信息。

papers.title: Oncolytic measles virus reprograms the tumor microenvironment in a vascularized mesothelioma-on-chip model
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is a rare and aggressive cancer primarily caused by asbestos exposure. Although dual immune checkpoint inhibition (anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4) is now approved as first-line therapy, clinical benefit is limited to a small subset of patients, necessitating the need for alternative strategies. Oncolytic viruses represent a promising therapeutic approach as they selectively infect and lyse tumor cells and display immunogenic properties. In PM, we showed that the oncolytic activity of measles virus (MV) is primarily dependent on alterations in the type I interferon (IFN-I) pathway. However, to date no in vitro models have yet been developed to mimic a sophisticated tumor microenvironment (TME), and accurately evaluate MV efficacy in PM. Methods We designed a humanized 3D “vascularized mesothelioma-on-chip” (VMOC) model using microfluidic chips that mimic a TME. VMOC are generated using primary endothelial cells, lung fibroblasts and patient-derived PM cells. We characterized the functionality of our model by confocal imaging, perfusion assay and single-cell RNA sequencing. The impact of MV on the VMOC was assessed by bulk transcriptomics, multiplex ELISA and deconvolution strategies, and compared to clinical data in patients with PM. Results We first proved VMOC functionality with an appropriate endothelial barrier integrity, perfusability, and vascular responsiveness to external stimuli. We demonstrated significant heterogeneity in the VMOC, with the presence of different mesenchymal, cancer and endothelial subpopulations. Interestingly, the addition of PM cells to the VMOC reduced both the IFN-I pathway in cells from the TME, and the abundance of a novel endothelial cell subset characterized by an IFN-I signaling signature. Following MV administration via the endothelial network, we detected PM cell infection and death, as well as strong activation of the IFN-I pathway with the production of multiple inflammatory mediators. Interestingly, the proteomic and transcriptomic inflammatory response induced by MV in VMOCs was similar to that induced in PM patients treated with an oncolytic virus. Conclusions The VMOC model we developed enables in vitro investigation of MV infection and TME reprogramming, paving the way for a deeper understanding of the TME role in OV responses and the development of novel strategies to improve clinical efficacy.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is a rare and aggressive cancer primarily caused by asbestos exposure. Although dual immune checkpoint inhibition (anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4) is now approved as first-line therapy, clinical benefit is limited to a small subset of patients, necessitating the need for alternative strategies. Oncolytic viruses represent a promising therapeutic approach as they selectively infect and lyse tumor cells and display immunogenic properties. In PM, we showed that the oncolytic activity of measles virus (MV) is primarily dependent on alterations in the type I interferon (IFN-I) pathway. However, to date no in vitro models have yet been developed to mimic a sophisticated tumor microenvironment (TME), and accurately evaluate MV efficacy in PM. Methods We designed a humanized 3D “vascularized mesothelioma-on-chip” (VMOC) model using microfluidic chips that mimic a TME. VMOC are generated using primary endothelial cells, lung fibroblasts and patient-derived PM cells. We characterized the functionality of our model by confocal imaging, perfusion assay and single-cell RNA sequencing. The impact of MV on the VMOC was assessed by bulk transcriptomics, multiplex ELISA and deconvolution strategies, and compared to clinical data in patients with PM. Results We first proved VMOC functionality with an appropriate endothelial barrier integrity, perfusability, and vascular responsiveness to external stimuli. We demonstrated significant heterogeneity in the VMOC, with the presence of different mesenchymal, cancer and endothelial subpopulations. Interestingly, the addition of PM cells to the VMOC reduced both the IFN-I pathway in cells from the TME, and the abundance of a novel endothelial cell subset characterized by an IFN-I signaling signature. Following MV administration via the endothelial network, we detected PM cell infection and death, as well as strong activation of the IFN-I pathway with the production of multiple inflammatory mediators. Interestingly, the proteomic and transcriptomic inflammatory response induced by MV in VMOCs was similar to that induced in PM patients treated with an oncolytic virus. Conclusions The VMOC model we developed enables in vitro investigation of MV infection and TME reprogramming, paving the way for a deeper understanding of the TME role in OV responses and the development of novel strategies to improve clinical efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of oncolytic measles virus (MV) in treating pleural mesothelioma (PM), a rare and aggressive cancer linked to asbestos exposure. The researchers developed a humanized 3D "vascularized mesothelioma-on-chip" (VMOC) model to mimic the tumor microenvironment (TME) and evaluate MV's efficacy. They demonstrated that MV's oncolytic activity is influenced by changes in the type I interferon (IFN-I) pathway. The VMOC model showed appropriate endothelial barrier integrity, perfusability, and vascular responsiveness, and revealed significant heterogeneity in the TME. The addition of PM cells to the VMOC reduced IFN-I pathway activity and altered the endothelial cell composition. MV administration led to PM cell infection and death, along with strong IFN-I pathway activation and production of inflammatory mediators. The proteomic and transcriptomic inflammatory response induced by MV in VMOCs mirrored that seen in PM patients treated with an oncolytic virus. The study highlights the potential of the VMOC model for investigating MV's effects on the TME and developing new therapeutic strategies. The findings are based on in vitro experiments and comparisons with clinical data, but the study does not report limitations or evidence strength.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 胸膜间皮瘤 (PM) 是一种罕见的侵袭性癌症,主要由石棉暴露引起。尽管双重免疫检查点抑制(抗 PD-1/抗 CTLA-4)现已被批准作为一线治疗,但临床获益仅限于一小部分患者,因此需要替代策略。溶瘤病毒代表了一种有前途的治疗方法,因为它们选择性地感染和裂解肿瘤细胞并表现出免疫原性。在 PM 中,我们发现 麻疹病毒 (MV) 的溶瘤活性主要依赖于 I 型干扰素 (IFN-I) 途径的改变。然而,迄今为止,尚未开发出体外模型来模拟复杂的肿瘤微环境 (TME),并准确评估 MV 对 PM 的疗效。方法我们使用模仿 TME 的微流控芯片设计了人性化 3D“芯片上血管化间皮瘤”(VMOC) 模型。VMOC 使用原代内皮细胞、肺成纤维细胞和患者来源的 PM 细胞产生。我们通过共聚焦成像、灌注测定和单细胞 RNA 测序来表征我们模型的功能。通过批量转录组学、多重 ELISA 和反卷积策略评估 MV 对 VMOC 的影响,并与 PM 患者的临床数据进行比较。结果我们首先证明了 VMOC 具有适当的内皮屏障完整性、可灌注性和血管对外部刺激的反应性的功能。我们证明了 VMOC 存在显着的异质性,存在不同的间充质、癌症和内皮亚群。有趣的是,将PM细胞添加到VMOC中既减少了来自TME的细胞中的IFN-I途径,也减少了以IFN-I信号传导特征为特征的新型内皮细胞亚群的丰度。通过内皮网络给予 MV 后,我们检测到 PM 细胞感染和死亡,以及 IFN-I 途径的强烈激活和多种炎症介质的产生。有趣的是,MV 在 VMOC 中诱导的蛋白质组和转录组炎症反应与用溶瘤病毒治疗的 PM 患者诱导的相似。结论 我们开发的 VMOC 模型能够对 MV 感染和 TME 重编程进行体外研究,为更深入地了解 TME 在 OV 反应中的作用以及开发提高临床疗效的新策略铺平道路。

papers.title: Measles ( rubeola) virus qualitative real-time reverse transcription–polymerase chain reaction assay: development and clinical validation on an automated workflow
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Detection of Measles virus (MeV) RNA is an important method for confirming infection. This study described the clinical validation of a qualitative real-time reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay for MeV detection. Methods A real-time RT-PCR assay was developed and validated using primers and probes previously reported in the literature. The assay was evaluated using reference materials, cultured virus, and previously tested clinical throat swab samples. An automated workflow was established for RNA extraction, RT-PCR amplification, and result reporting using robotic platforms and a real-time PCR instrument. The assay targets the measles nucleoprotein (N) and hemagglutinin (H) genes, with human RNase P gene used as an internal control. Results The MeV RT-PCR assay has a limit of detection of 500 genome copies per milliliter. The assay was tested against 85 different samples: 50 positive clinical samples and reference materials and 35 negative clinical samples or reference materials. All expected results were correctly identified, giving 100% sensitivity (50/50) and specificity (35/35). The assay showed 100% interassay and intra-assay reproducibility. No cross-reactivity was observed with other respiratory viruses or common bacterial and fungal pathogens. papers.title: Epidemiological, Clinical, and Clinical Course Profile of Measles during the 2023–2024 Outbreak in Burkina Faso
papers.abstract: Introduction: Measles is a widespread exanthematous febrile illness caused by a paramyxovirus of the genus Morbillivirus. The reservoir is exclusively human, and transmission occurs between humans. It is one of the most contagious infectious diseases. In Burkina Faso, measles remains a public health problem. The country experienced a major epidemic from November 2023 to August 2024. Objective: To study the epidemiological, clinical, and disease-progression profile of measles during the 2023–2024 epidemic in Burkina Faso. Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study used data on measles cases reported in Burkina Faso from 1 November 2023 to 31 August 2024. The data were obtained from the database of the Directorate of Population Health Protection. Descriptive analysis was performed using Excel 2019. Results: A total of 7,149 measles cases were included. The overall incidence of measles was 33.28 per 100,000 inhabitants. Males were overrepresented, accounting for 51.45% of cases. The median age was 4 years. The most frequently represented age group was 0–5 years, accounting for 55.81% of cases. Most measles cases were unvaccinated, accounting for 55.31% of cases. The Hauts-Bassins and Centre regions were the most affected, with incidence rates of 67.78 and 60.17 cases per 100,000 inhabitants, respectively. The health districts of Houndé (14.69%) in the Hauts-Bassins region and Bogodogo (10.77%) in the Centre region reported the highest numbers of cases. Epidemiological weeks S08-2024 and S12-2024 recorded the highest numbers of measles cases, accounting for 7.33% and 7.32% of cases, respectively. Only 11.87% of cases had travelled within the seven days before the onset of clinical symptoms. Fever, rash, and cough were the most commonly reported symptoms, occurring in 96.87%, 95.06%, and 89.29% of cases, respectively. Laboratory confirmation was obtained in 9.79% of cases. The measles case-fatality rate during the outbreak was 0.45%. Conclusion: Measles remains a public health problem, underscoring the need to strengthen the Expanded Programme on Immunization, outbreak response, and nationwide vaccination strategies.

papers.title: SVIR Model Analysis of Measles with Incomplete Vaccination and 1 Waning Immunity: Sidoarjo-Indonesia Case
papers.abstract: Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity. This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity. The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions. Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods. The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime. papers.abstract_zh: 麻疹仍然是印度尼西亚的重大公共卫生挑战,尤其是在疫苗接种覆盖率异质性和免疫力下降的地区。本研究开发并分析了一个针对麻疹传播的易感-接种-感染-康复(SVIR)分组模型,该模型纳入了免疫力下降的因素。基本再生数R0是通过下一代矩阵方法推导的,并且通过李雅普诺夫函数严格证明了无病平衡态和地方性平衡态的全局稳定性。模型参数是从2023年Sidoarjo市每周的监测数据中使用粒子群优化(PSO)、扩展卡尔曼滤波、最大似然估计和最小二乘法进行估计,并通过平均绝对百分比误差(MAPE)进行评估。PSO方法实现了最低的MAPE(11.17%),优于其他方法。估计的R0 = 0.668确认了无病状态。归一化敏感性分析确定疫苗效力是最关键的参数;疫苗效力下降至0 .75会使R0接近临界阈值,任何进一步的减少都会使系统进入地方性状态。这些发现强调了通过加强剂接种计划和强化疫苗接种策略保持高疫苗效力的必要性,以在区级维持麻疹的消除。

papers.title: Optimal Control and Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Measles Transmission
papers.abstract: This study develops and analyzes a deterministic compartmental model for measles transmission incorporating two-dose vaccination, imperfect dose-specific vaccine protection, breakthrough infection, and nonlinear saturated incidence. The population is divided into susceptible, first-dose vaccinated, second-dose vaccinated, exposed, infectious, and recovered classes. The fundamental mathematical properties of the model are established, including positivity and boundedness of solutions. The disease-free and endemic equilibria are characterized, and the basic reproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix approach. The disease-free equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable when R0 1 the model admits a unique endemic equilibrium that is globally asymptotically stable relative to the interior of the biologically feasible region. Analytical sensitivity analysis identifies the local influence of the model parameters on R0. In particular, the saturation parameter does not enter R0, but numerical analysis shows that it can substantially affect the endemic infection level. The model is further extended to an optimal-control framework with three time-dependent, dimensionless controls representing intensified first-dose vaccination, intensified second-dose vaccination, and enhanced infectious-case removal. The existence of an optimal control is established, and Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle is used to derive the necessary optimality conditions. The resulting state–adjoint system is solved numerically using the Forward–Backward Sweep Method. Numerical simulations show that the combined optimal intervention reduces the exposed and infectious disease burdens over the finite control horizon, while sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the optimal-control profiles depend on the relative weights assigned to disease burden and intervention effort. Seven intervention combinations are subsequently compared using the model-based Average Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ACER) and Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) measures. Under the baseline weighting scheme, first-dose vaccination alone has the smallest weighted intervention effort per case averted. After strong and extended dominance are accounted for, the incremental frontier consists of first-dose vaccination alone, first-dose vaccination combined with infectious-case removal, and the full three-control strategy. Increasing epidemiological benefit along this frontier is accompanied by increasing incremental weighted intervention effort. These results illustrate how dose-specific vaccination, nonlinear transmission, and infectious-case intervention can be integrated within a unified framework for comparing measles-control strategies while explicitly accounting for the assumptions underlying intervention effort.

The research aims to evaluate optimal control strategies for measles disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The population is divided into susceptible, first-dose vaccinated, second-dose vaccinated, exposed, infectious, and recovered classes. The study is conducted using a mathematical modeling approach to simulate measles transmission dynamics.
analysis.methods: The fundamental mathematical properties of the model are established, including positivity and boundedness of solutions. The disease-free and endemic equilibria are characterized, and the basic reproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix approach. The model is further extended to an optimal-control framework with three time-dependent, dimensionless controls representing intensified first-dose vaccination, intensified second-dose vaccination, and enhanced infectious-case removal.
analysis.main_results: The disease-free equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable when R0 < 1, and the model admits a unique endemic equilibrium that is globally asymptotically stable relative to the interior of the biologically feasible region. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform the development of cost-effective measles-control strategies by highlighting the importance of dose-specific vaccination and the integration of infectious-case interventions. analysis.summary_en: This study develops a deterministic compartmental model for measles transmission, incorporating two-dose vaccination, imperfect vaccine protection, breakthrough infection, and nonlinear incidence. The model is extended to an optimal-control framework with three interventions: intensified first-dose vaccination, intensified second-dose vaccination, and enhanced infectious-case removal. The disease-free equilibrium is globally stable when R0 < 1, and the endemic equilibrium is stable within the biologically feasible region. Numerical simulations show that combined optimal interventions reduce disease burden, while sensitivity analysis reveals that intervention profiles depend on the relative weights of disease burden and effort. The study highlights the integration of dose-specific vaccination and infectious-case interventions within a unified framework for evaluating measles-control strategies. The findings can inform cost-effective public health interventions but are based on theoretical models and may not fully reflect real-world complexities.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究开发并分析了 麻疹 传播 的确定性隔室模型,该模型包含两剂量 疫苗接种、不完善的剂量特异性 疫苗 保护、突破性感染和非线性饱和 发病率。该研究旨在评估 麻疹 疾病的最佳控制策略。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 人群分为易感人群、第一剂疫苗接种者、第二剂疫苗接种者、暴露者、感染者和康复者。该研究是使用数学建模方法来模拟 麻疹 传播 动力学进行的。
elements_zh.methods: 建立了模型的基本数学属性,包括解的正性和有界性。对无病和地方病平衡进行了表征,并使用下一代矩阵方法推导出基本再生数 R0。该模型进一步扩展到具有三个时间依赖性无量纲控制的最优控制框架,这三个控制代表强化的第一剂量 疫苗接种、强化的第二剂量 疫苗接种 和增强的感染病例清除。
elements_zh.main_results: 当 R0 < 1 时,无病平衡是全局渐近稳定的,并且该模型承认独特的地方性平衡,相对于生物学可行区域的内部来说,该平衡是全局渐近稳定的。数值模拟表明,组合的最佳干预措施可以减少有限控制范围内的暴露疾病和传染病负担。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果说明了如何将剂量特异性 疫苗接种、非线性 传播 和感染病例干预整合到一个统一的框架中,以比较 麻疹 控制策略,同时明确考虑干预工作的假设。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以通过强调特定剂量 麻疹 和感染病例干预措施整合的重要性,为制定具有成本效益的 麻疹 控制策略提供信息。它们为评估不同 疫苗接种 方案对疾病 传播 的影响提供了基础。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于数学模型,并未考虑现实世界的复杂性,例如行为变化或空间异质性。证据来自理论分析和数值模拟,可能无法完全捕捉生物变异性。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 人群分为易感人群、第一剂疫苗接种者、第二剂疫苗接种者、暴露者、感染者和康复者。该研究是使用数学建模方法来模拟 麻疹 传播 动力学进行的。

papers.abstract: We developed a measles transmission model for K-12 public schools in Texas at the school-district-level. papers.title: An age-stratified mathematical model to inform optimal measles vaccination strategies
papers.abstract: Background: Measles remains a significant global public health threat despite the availability of an effective vaccine. WHO recommends the first measles vaccine dose at 9–12 months of age, balancing maternal antibody interference and immune system maturity. However, infants younger than 9 months remain highly vulnerable, especially in regions with high transmission and low herd immunity. Methods: This study introduces an age-stratified, multi-compartmental model of measles transmission that captures infections in unvaccinated infants by explicitly modelling maternal immunity decay and early infection risks. We prove the model’s positivity and derive an analytical expression for the instantaneous replacement number. For a non-age-stratified version, we analyze equilibrium points and their stability. We also conducted a global sensitivity analysis of the model parameters with respect to the aggregate incidence of measles over 30 years. Further, using a bootstrap algorithm, critical parameters and age-specific transmission rates are identified by fitting the model to yearly incidence data from six measles-prevalent countries. papers.abstract_zh: 背景:尽管存在有效的 麻疹,但 麻疹 仍然是一个重大的全球公共卫生威胁。世卫组织建议在 9-12 个月龄时首次注射 麻疹 疫苗,以平衡母体抗体干扰和免疫系统成熟度。然而,9 个月以下的婴儿仍然非常脆弱,特别是在 传播 高且群体免疫力低的地区。方法:本研究引入了 麻疹 传播 的年龄分层、多室模型,该模型通过明确模拟母体免疫力衰退和早期感染风险来捕获未接种疫苗的婴儿的感染。我们证明了模型的正性并推导出瞬时替换数的解析表达式。对于非年龄分层版本,我们分析平衡点及其稳定性。我们还对模型参数相对于 30 年来 麻疹 的总和 发病率 进行了全局敏感性分析。此外,使用引导算法,通过将模型拟合到六个 麻疹 流行国家的年度 发病率 数据来确定关键参数和特定年龄的 传播 率。结果:1-5岁儿童中的传播与累积麻疹 发病率具有最强的正相关性,而MCV1疗效和覆盖率具有最强的负相关性。2020 年至 2023 年期间估计瞬时更换数量在 0.85 至 1.15 之间波动。在模型假设下,包含 MCV0 的场景比不包含 MCV0 的场景产生的预计 麻疹 发病率 的减少幅度更大。所提出的模型提供了一个用于评估假设的 疫苗接种 场景的框架,包括不同的常规和补充剂量方案。结论:该研究估计了避免病例的相对数量,并预测了几种假设情况下的消除时间表,强调将常规免疫和补充免疫与早期 麻疹 疫苗接种 等替代假设相结合可能非常有效。

papers.title: Genetic characterization of production strains of measles, rubella, and mumps viruses by high-throughput sequencing
papers.abstract: Spontaneous mutations often arise and accumulate in the genome of RNA-containing viruses, for example measles, rubella and mumps. Modern requirements for the production of vaccine products containing live vaccine viruses suggest control of the genetic stability of production strains. The method of high throughput sequencing allows to determine all mutations arisen in viral population, and to assess genetic stability of production strains. analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess the genetic stability of measles, rubella, and mumps production strains using high-throughput sequencing. The research focused on identifying mutations in the viral genomes that could impact vaccine immunogenicity. The study revealed that measles virus production strains had no SNPs in the H protein but showed nonsynonymous polymorphisms in the F protein, occurring in 30.0–40.9% of the viral genomes. papers.title: Gaps in Knowledge, Receipt, and Acceptance of Measles, Mumps, Rubella Vaccines in a National Sample of Emergency Department
papers.abstract: Measles cases are increasing in the U.S., raising concern about gaps in adult measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccination, which is poorly captured by current surveillance. Emergency departments (EDs) act as safety nets for underserved populations and can help identify gaps in adult MMR uptake. We assessed adult MMR up-to-date status, knowledge, and willingness to receive vaccination in the ED, nationally. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of adults aged 18–64 at ten U.S. EDs from April–December 2024. Participants completed a structured survey assessing MMR knowledge, self-reported vaccination status, reasons for non-receipt, and willingness to receive MMR in the ED. Outcomes were summarized as proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with not being up to date and willingness to accept vaccination. Among 2,456 participants, 25.0% (95% CI 23.3–26.7%) had not heard of the MMR vaccine, and 44.0% (42.5–46.4%) were not up to date. Factors associated with being unvaccinated included male sex (OR 2.21 [1.84–2.66]), African American (non-Hispanic) race (OR 2.27 [1.75–2.96]), Hispanic ethnicity (OR 1.98 [1.49–2.62]), non-English speakers (OR 1.53 [1.12–2.09]), and lack of primary care access (OR 1.25 [1.01–1.58]). Among those not up to date, 36.5% (33.6–39.4%) were willing to receive MMR vaccine if offered in the ED. Substantial gaps in adult MMR vaccination persist, especially among underserved populations. ED-based strategies might support targeted vaccine education and delivery during periods of increased transmission.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess gaps in adult measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccination, knowledge, and willingness to receive the vaccine in emergency departments (EDs). A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 2,456 adults aged 18–64 at ten U.S. EDs from April to December 2024. The survey evaluated MMR knowledge, self-reported vaccination status, reasons for non-receipt, and willingness to accept vaccination. Results showed that 25.0% of participants had not heard of the MMR vaccine, and 44.0% were not up to date. Among those not up to date, 36.5% expressed willingness to receive the vaccine if offered in the ED. The authors suggest that ED-based strategies could support targeted vaccine education and delivery during periods of increased transmission. The study highlights the importance of addressing vaccination gaps in underserved populations, particularly those with limited access to primary care. However, the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit the confidence in the findings, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title: Active measles surveillance in the Russian Federation: implementation principles and current challenges
papers.abstract: From 2004 to 2006, a pilot project was carried out in 11 territories of the Russian Federation to test the method of active epidemiological surveillance, which makes it possible to identify the true number of measles patients among persons with maculopapular rash and fever, regardless of the primary diagnosis. To provide a clinical and epidemiological characterization of measles cases detected through active surveillance and to assess the quality of pre-hospital diagnosis. Materials and Methods. A retrospective analysis of data from 2017–2025 was conducted, including 1.691 epidemiological investigation forms for patients identified through active surveillance and 2.517 hospital records of inpatients. papers.title: Measles transmission and surveillance in open subcommunities
papers.abstract: We're often in a situation where we have models of measles transmission that are stuck at a coarse population scale. This paper is about increasing their resolution or, said differently, creating consistent models for the population's subcommunities. We pay special attention to the fact that even if the full population is isolated, subcommunities are open to measles importations and related consequences of population movement. It turns out that the resolution issue can be productively framed as a constrained optimization problem, where the constraint is aggregation to the coarse model. That mathematical scaffolding allows us to make epidemiologically motivated approximations concentrated at the large population scale, where they're more valid, which leaves the estimates at the fine subcommunity scale atypically unstructured. We develop the idea in the context of the pre-vaccination-era 60 city UK dataset, building transmission models for all 60 cities. We find that they have intuitive seasonality, volatility, and importation elements, but that they depend on nontrivial dynamics in their case reporting probabilities. Potential interpretations of those surveillance processes are discussed in some detail, and we also describe how they influence inference on the balance between competing cryptic transmission and transient elimination dynamics.

papers.title: Sốt phát ban nghi sởi tại Nghệ An năm 2024–2025: Phân bố theo nhóm tuổi nguy cơ và địa bàn xã mới từ số liệu giám sát Suspected Measles Cases in Nghe An during 2024–2025: A descriptive analysis of age group and new communes based on surveillance data
papers.abstract: Năm 2024-2025, Nghệ An ghi nhận số trường hợp SPB nghi sởi cao vượt mức so với trung bình giai đoạn 2019-2023. Nghiên cứu loạt ca bệnh hồi cứu nhằm mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ, tập trung vào sự phân bố theo thời gian, nhóm tuổi và địa bàn xã mới thông qua hệ thống giám sát từ 01/2024 - 12/2025. Kết quả ghi nhận 4.531 ca SPB nghi sởi, (từ 0-81 tuổi), tập trung ở trẻ<5 tuổi (nhóm từ 2- <5 tuổi chiếm tỷ trọng cao nhất 27,8%). Nhóm ≥ 5 tuổi (chiếm 40,5%), cho thấy bệnh đã xuất hiện nhiều ở các nhóm tuổi lớn hơn, phản ánh sự tồn tại của khoảng trống miễn dịch trong cộng đồng. 588/712 ca sởi xét nghiệm dương tính (82,6%) cho thấy 100% có sốt, phát ban, 99,5% biến chứng viêm phổi và 86,7% chưa tiêm vắc xin sởi. Các xã có tỷ lệ mắc cao nhất chủ yếu ở vùng cao, biên giới. Theo thời gian, số mắc tăng dần vào nửa cuối năm 2024 và đạt đỉnh vào tháng 3/2025 (1.296 trường hợp), sau đó giảm dần. Cần ưu tiên nguồn lực dự phòng cho các xã khó khăn, đẩy mạnh truyền thông nguy cơ phù hợp với đặc điểm văn hoá, ngôn ngữ của đồng bào dân tộc thiểu số về lợi ích của vắc-xin, vận động người dân tham gia tiêm chủng, đồng thời duy trì hệ thống dữ liệu giám sát chặt chẽ.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Năm 2024–2025, Nghệ An ghi nhận số trường hợp sốt phát ban nghi sởi cao vượt mức so với trung bình giai đoạn 2019–2023. Nghiên cứu này nhằm mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ của bệnh, tập trung vào sự phân bố theo thời gian, nhóm tuổi và địa bàn xã mới.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Nghiên cứu loạt ca bệnh hồi cứu được thực hiện tại Nghệ An từ 01/2024 đến 12/2025, tập trung vào các ca bệnh sốt phát ban nghi sởi được ghi nhận qua hệ thống giám sát. Tổng cộng có 4.531 ca được ghi nhận, bao gồm cả trẻ em dưới 5 tuổi và người lớn hơn.
analysis.methods: Kết quả được thu thập từ hệ thống giám sát, mô tả phân bố theo nhóm tuổi và địa bàn xã. Các ca bệnh được phân loại dựa trên lứa tuổi và khu vực địa lý, đồng thời xác định tỷ lệ mắc bệnh theo thời gian.
analysis.main_results: Trong tổng số 4.531 ca SPB nghi sởi, trẻ dưới 5 tuổi chiếm tỷ trọng cao nhất (27,8%), trong khi nhóm ≥ 5 tuổi chiếm 40,5%. Số ca mắc tăng dần vào nửa cuối năm 2024 và đạt đỉnh vào tháng 3/2025 (1.296 trường hợp), sau đó giảm dần.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Sự gia tăng số ca mắc ở các nhóm tuổi lớn hơn cho thấy sự tồn tại của khoảng trống miễn dịch trong cộng đồng, điều này có thể phản ánh sự suy giảm tỷ lệ tiêm chủng. Các xã có tỷ lệ mắc cao nhất chủ yếu ở vùng cao và biên giới.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Kết quả cho thấy cần ưu tiên nguồn lực dự phòng cho các xã có tỷ lệ mắc cao, đặc biệt là ở vùng cao và biên giới, đồng thời đẩy mạnh truyền thông về lợi ích của vắc-xin sởi.

analysis.summary_en: The study analyzed measles-like cases in Nghe An during 2024–2025, revealing a higher incidence compared to 2019–2023. It focused on the distribution of cases by age group and new communes, identifying a significant proportion in children under 5 and a rising trend in late 2024. The findings highlight the presence of immune gaps in the population and emphasize the need for targeted prevention in high-risk areas. The research underscores the importance of strengthening surveillance and promoting vaccination, particularly among ethnic minority communities. However, the study is limited to descriptive analysis based on surveillance data without detailed statistical or laboratory methods.

papers.title: Đặc điểm dịch tễ học bệnh sởi và xác định các cụm nguy cơ cao mắc bệnh theo không gian–thời gian bằng phương pháp thống kê quét tại tỉnh Đắk Nông, năm 2024–2025 The epidemiological characteristics and the application of scan statistics to identify highrisk space–time clusters of the measles outbreak in Dak Nong province, 2024–2025
papers.abstract: Nghiên cứu mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ học và xác định các cụm nguy cơ cao mắc bệnh theo không gian – thờigian của các trường hợp sốt phát ban nghi sởi và sởi xác định tại Đắk Nông năm 2024 – 2025. Nghiên cứucắt ngang hồi cứu dựa trên số liệu giám sát, kết hợp phân tích không gian – thời gian. Có 852/869 trườnghợp đủ thông tin được đưa vào phân tích. Thống kê quét được thực hiện bằng phần mềm SaTScan vớimô hình Poisson rời rạc, cửa sổ không gian tối đa 10% dân số nguy cơ, cửa sổ thời gian tối đa 21 ngàyvà 9.999 lần mô phỏng Monte Carlo. Dịch sởi diễn biến thành hai đợt tăng chính vào nửa cuối 2024 vàđầu 2025, 68,2% trường hợp ghi nhận trong năm 2025. Trẻ dưới 15 tuổi chiếm 89,2%, trong đó nhóm 18tháng đến 5 tuổi chiếm tỷ lệ cao nhất (32,0%). Người Kinh, Mông và Mnông lần lượt chiếm 46,8%, 30,9%và 11,6%. Hơn 70% xã/phường có tỷ suất mắc từ 50/100.000 dân trở lên. Phân tích SaTScan xác định19 cụm nguy cơ cao có ý nghĩa thống kê, RR dao động từ 5,32 đến 177,93, chủ yếu xuất hiện từ tháng8/2024 đến tháng 4/2025, phù hợp với hai đợt tăng chính của dịch. Cụm nổi bật nhất tại Đắk Ngo từ ngày10–30/9/2024, có 76 trường hợp, RR = 177,93 và p < 0,0001. Kết quả cho thấy các trường hợp bệnh phânbố không đồng đều theo không gian và thời gian. SaTScan hỗ trợ xác định địa bàn và thời điểm cần ưu tiênhỗ trợ trong giám sát chủ động, điều tra ổ dịch, rà soát tiêm chủng và triển khai tiêm vét.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to describe the epidemiological characteristics and identify high-risk space-time clusters of measles outbreaks in Dak Nong province during 2024–2025. It employed a cross-sectional retrospective study design using surveillance data combined with space-time scan analysis. The methods included the use of SaTScan software with a discrete Poisson model, a spatial window of up to 10% of the at-risk population, a temporal window of up to 21 days, and 9,999 Monte Carlo simulations. The main results showed that measles outbreaks occurred in two main waves towards the end of 2024 and the beginning of 2025, with 68.2% of cases recorded in 2025. The analysis identified 19 statistically significant high-risk clusters, with relative risks ranging from 5.32 to 177.93, primarily appearing from August 2024 to April 2025, aligning with the two main outbreak waves. The most prominent cluster was in Dak Nong from September 10–30, 2024, with 76 cases, RR = 177.93, and p < 0.0001. The findings indicate uneven spatial and temporal distribution of measles cases. SaTScan results support targeted efforts in active surveillance, outbreak investigation, vaccination review, and mass vaccination campaigns. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of reported limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines long-term survival (≥2 years) in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), a severe neurological complication of measles virus infection. The review aimed to characterize prolonged survivors, remission, and stabilization, and identify factors influencing favorable outcomes. Based on analysis of 77 patients, survival beyond 2 years is possible but highly variable. The survival distribution showed that 44.2% of patients survived between 2 to [incomplete data]. The evidence is limited by incomplete data on survival distribution, which hinders a comprehensive understanding of long-term outcomes. The findings suggest the need for further research to explore the determinants of favorable outcomes and to improve surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for SSPE patients.

papers.full_text: Nature Reviews Microbiology nature reviews microbiology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41579-026-01372-1 Review article Check for updates Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses Hendrik Jan Thibaut 1, Dirk Jochmans 1,3, Christophe Van Dijck2,3, Manon Laporte 1,3, Laurens Liesenborghs 2 & Johan Neyts1 Abstract Small molecule antiviral drugs have transformed the management of infections such as those caused by HIV, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, herpesviruses and influenza viruses. Effective antiviral therapeutics remain unavailable for many other often life-threatening viral infections, many of which are caused by RNA viruses. The development of potent, safe and orally available antivirals is therefore essential both to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for building a diversified portfolio of broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses with activity spanning multiple genera, entire families or even crossing viral families. We provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses and discuss the biological determinants that underlie their antiviral spectrum. Finally, we outline the clinical development frameworks required to accelerate the evaluation of such drugs, in particular in the context of outbreaks. Sections Introduction One drug to treat them all? Direct-acting antivirals versus host-targeting antivirals New approaches to discover new targets for broader-acting antivirals Translational readiness Conclusions 1KU Leuven Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Transplantation, Antiviral Drug and Vaccine Research Group, Leuven, Belgium. 2Department of Clinical Sciences, Institute of Tropical Medicine, Antwerp, Belgium. 3These authors contributed equally: Dirk Jochmans, Christophe Van Dijck, Manon Laporte. e-mail: johan.neyts@kuleuven.be Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article Alongside vaccine development, sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery is therefore essential. Antiviral drug development has so far largely been focused on viral infections that offer large and predict- able commercial markets (for example, those caused by HIV and HCV). It is obviously unrealistic and economically unsustainable to develop specific antiviral drugs for each known viral pathogen. Newly emerging viruses will most likely belong to viral families already known (Table 1) today. Advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing greatly expanded our understanding of viral diversity, and although new viral families may still be discovered, such events are becoming increasingly rare. Together, this strongly supports a strategy in which broader-acting small molecule antiviral (BSA) drugs are developed. Such drugs can be used for the treatment and prophylaxis of infec- tions with known viruses for which no antiviral treatment is available and, in the case of epidemics or pandemics, as a rapid response option while other countermeasures, such as vaccines and mAbs, are being developed12,13. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for the development of BSAs and provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved or experi- mental antiviral drugs active against viruses with an RNA genome. We also outline strategies for target discovery and accelerated clinical development. One drug to treat them all? The term ‘broad-spectrum’ antiviral has been widely used but lacks, to the best of our knowledge, a clear definition. Here, we propose instead to use the term ‘broader-spectrum’ antivirals and distinguish three categories: (i) cross-family BSAs with activity across unrelated viral families within or across a certain genome architecture, that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA); (ii) pan-family BSAs that act across the different genera of a given viral family (for example, pan-paramyxovirus drugs); and (iii) intra-family BSAs, which are active against multiple serotypes and genotypes of a particular virus (for example, pan-serotype dengue virus (DENV) Introduction Viruses, whether known or yet to emerge (‘virus X’), remain a major threat to global health. Vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and antiviral drugs are each important and complementary in controlling viral infections. Vaccination has led to the eradication of smallpox, brought polio close to eradication and massively reduced disease and mortality associated with numerous viral infections, such as measles virus, mumps virus, rubella virus, influenza virus, severe acute respira- tory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human papillomavirus1–3. For several important human pathogens, such as HIV, hepatitis C virus (HCV), herpes simplex viruses (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), rhinoviruses and many others, the devel- opment of highly effective vaccines has proved difficult or remains elusive, often despite decades of intensive effort. Therefore, it cannot be guaranteed that efficacious vaccines can always be developed when new threatening viruses emerge4,5. mAbs can offer immediate protection and are transforming the prophylaxis or treatment of certain acute viral diseases, such as those caused by the rabies virus6 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)7. They generally have an excellent safety profile and can be highly effective, although they require injections, are virus specific or variant spe- cific and can rapidly select for escape variants8,9. Like vaccines, mAbs can be developed only once a new pathogen has been identified and characterized. By contrast, small molecule antiviral drugs offer several distinct advantages. They can be administered orally and have the potential to cover a broader spectrum of viruses (Box 1) than vaccines and mAbs. Antiviral drugs have revolutionized the treatment of certain (chronic) viral infections such as those caused by either HIV, HBV, HCV, HSV-1 and HSV-2, and CMV. More recently, antiviral drugs have also become availa- ble against some other viruses including influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2 and hepatitis delta virus. However, for the majority of the more than 200 known human pathogenic viruses, no antiviral drugs are available. Most of these viruses are RNA viruses — the focus of this Review — including many emerging and clinically important pathogens10–12. Box 1 | Categories and examples of broader-spectrum antivirals (BSAs) for RNA viruses Cross-family BSAs Active against viruses belonging to different (related or unrelated) viral families or across a certain genome architecture (that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA viruses)), typically by targeting conserved features of the viral replication machinery such as the catalytic site of viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases. For example, remdesivir, a nucleoside viral polymerase inhibitor, is active against viruses belonging to different viral families, that is, the (−)ssRNA Filoviridae, Paramyxoviridae, Pneumoviridae and Arenaviridae as well as the (+) ssRNA Flaviviridae, Picornaviridae and Coronaviridae. Baloxavir, an endonuclease inhibitor, inhibits influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae) but also, although much less potently, several members of the family Peribunyaviridae. Pan-family BSAs Active across all or at least most genera within a single viral family. Examples include neuraminidase inhibitors such as oseltamivir, zanamivir and peramivir that are active against both influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae). Nirmatrelvir is a reversible covalent, peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor that inhibits human and animal coronaviruses belonging to different genera within the family Coronaviridae. Intra-family BSAs Can be active against multiple serotypes, genotypes or strains of a particular virus species. For example, mosnodenvir is active against all dengue virus genotypes (family Flaviviridae) by blocking the interaction between viral proteins NS4B and NS3. Intra-family broader-spectrum activity may span several viruses within one genus of a particular family without extending to other genera. For example, the non-covalent, non-peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor ensitrelvir is active only against members of the genus Betacoronavirus (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), SARS-CoV-1 and human coronavirus (HCoV)-OC43), but not against members of the genus Alphacoronavirus (such as HCoV-229E and HCoV-NL63) within the family Coronaviridae. Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article inhibitors) or active against one or more (but not all) genera of a viral family (Box 1). The need for broader-acting antivirals and their desired spectrum of activity are mostly defined by the particular (clinical) context (Boxes 2 and 3). For viruses that cause a high number of annual cases (for example, RSV), there might be a sufficiently large market, and thus incentives, to develop virus-specific drugs. Conversely, there might be no or less financial incentive to develop virus-specific drugs for viruses that cause a rather limited number of cases but that col- lectively, within their genus or family, are responsible for a substan- tial clinical burden (for example, coxsackieviruses and echoviruses, EV-D68 and EV-A71 that all belong to the genus Enterovirus). In this case, the development of antivirals that are broadly active across the entire Enterovirus genus (pan-Enterovirus; category intra-family BSAs) represents a more realistic approach. In the context of epidemic or pan- demic preparedness, access to pan-family and cross-family BSAs may be particularly important, as it cannot be predicted which viral family a newly emerging pathogen (‘virus X’) will belong to. Given the extensive genetic diversity and distinct replication strategies of viral families, the development of a single cross-family drug with potent activity against all RNA virus families is likely to be unrealistic. Rather, a more feasible strategy may be to establish a portfolio of different types of BSAs that collectively provide, either alone or in combination, coverage across the RNA virus landscape. BSAs may also be valuable in the context of viral co-infections, in which a single drug could simultaneously target two (or more) viruses14,15. Beyond the spectrum of activity, BSA development must be guided by clearly defined target product profiles16. To have a meaningful clinical impact, BSAs (or combinations thereof) should ideally be highly efficacious, be orally available (preferably once daily dosing), be safe for a broad patient population (preferably including pregnant women and children), possess a (relatively) high barrier to resistance and exhibit minimal drug–drug interactions16. Virus tissue tropism further influences desirable drug properties. For example, infections involving the central nervous system require efficient blood–brain barrier penetration, whereas limited penetration may be preferable for peripheral viral infections. Consequently, distinct target product profiles may be required, even within a single viral genus. TBEV, tick-borne encephalitis virus. Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article typically invade the central nerve system, whereas yellow fever virus and DENV do not17. The importance of preparedness against known viruses (such as EV-D6818, Ebola virus19, monkeypox virus20 and Andes hantavirus21) as well as against emerging viral threats (for example, SARS-CoV-2) has been repeatedly illustrated during outbreaks caused by these diverse viral pathogens. During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19 pan- demic), no antiviral drugs were available at the onset. A stockpile of an oral, pan-family coronavirus BSA before the start of the COVID-19 pan- demic would likely have saved countless lives22,23. Remdesivir, originally discovered as an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) inhibitor of RSV24 and Ebola viruses25,26, was the only drug for which antiviral activity against coronaviruses had been systematically demonstrated in preclinical models before the pandemic27. In the absence of readily available and effective antiviral treat- ments, drug repurposing may need to be considered. Repurpos- ing can provide a rapid and relatively cost-effective response by leveraging de-risked drugs with existing preclinical and clinical safety data28,29. However, drugs developed or used for non-viral indi- cations are mostly unlikely to possess sufficient antiviral potency to curb outbreaks caused by newly emerging and (potentially highly) pathogenic viruses. At the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, extensive repurposing initiatives studied whether drugs approved for other indications could inhibit SARS-CoV-2 replication. Drugs such as azithro- mycin (antibiotic), itraconazole (antifungal), hydroxychloroquine (antimalarial, antirheumatic), niclosamide (anthelmintic), ivermectin (anthelmintic) and nitazoxanide (antiparasitic) rapidly entered numer- ous clinical trials, many of them small and underpowered, and even became, for some time, standard treatment in certain settings despite limited preclinical evidence30. Overall, drug repurposing efforts dur- ing the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic were largely unsuccessful, highlighting that such strategies should not be initiated only at the time a new virus emerges. A more realistic approach is to systematically assess existing drugs during epidemic or pandemic ‘peace-time’ against panels of viruses that are representative of high-risk families. Drugs with ‘reason- able’ in vitro activity can be further tested, alone or in combinations, in preclinical models13. Studies in SARS-CoV-2-infected hamsters revealed that combi- nations of two or three antivirals, each used at suboptimal or even inactive doses, can result in important antiviral effects31. To ration- ally develop combination strategies for BSAs, systematic preclinical testing of combinations across viral families is required. Extensive preclinical studies of the most promising combinations may help to guide strategies for stockpiling for epidemic or pandemic prepared- ness. The use of fixed-dose combinations (such as those used in the treatment of HIV infections) would be ideal. Yet, in outbreak situation with new pathogens, there will be insufficient time to develop such fixed-dose combinations; co-administration of individual drugs would therefore represent a more practical approach.
