elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 疫苗接种 对于儿童自身免疫性和自身炎症性风湿病 (pedAIIRD) 的治疗具有临床意义,但具有挑战性。该研究旨在就 疫苗接种 对接受免疫抑制治疗的 pedAIIRD 儿童的安全性、免疫原性和有效性产生临床适用的真实世界证据。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 五项研究涉及三个 疫苗 平台:减毒活 麻疹-腮腺炎-风疹 (MMR) 加强剂 疫苗、COVID-19 mRNA 疫苗 和重组带状疱疹 疫苗(RZV;Shingrix)。对 186 名幼年特发性关节炎 (JIA) 儿童的 队列研究 进行了 MMR 增强剂 疫苗接种 的评估,并对 157 名儿科风湿病儿童的前瞻性 队列研究 进行了 COVID-19 mRNA 疫苗接种 的研究。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了系统回顾和荟萃分析,以评估 COVID-19 疫苗接种 与儿童多系统炎症综合征 (MIS-C) 之间的关联。一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究用于评估患有儿科风湿性疾病的儿童对 mRNA 疫苗 的体液和 T 细胞反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 186 名幼年特发性关节炎 (JIA) 儿童的 队列研究 试验中,MMR 增强剂 疫苗 与疾病活动性增加无关,并且没有观察到与 疫苗 相关的严重不良事件。对 182 名 JIA 儿童的长期评估表明,大多数患者保留了针对 麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹的保护性抗体。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,选定的活体疫苗可以安全地用于患有免疫介导的炎症性疾病的儿童,并且有必要对长期疫苗诱导的免疫进行有针对性的监测。结果还表明,即使接受生物治疗的患者的抗体浓度较低,mRNA 疫苗 在此人群中也是有效的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可能有助于未来国家和国际 疫苗接种 针对免疫介导的炎症性疾病儿童的建议,支持从广泛的 疫苗 避免转向个体化、治疗 特定的 疫苗接种 策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些证据基于观察性研究和系统评价,可能会受到偏见和混杂因素的影响。然而,这些发现得到了大型 队列研究 和多项研究的支持,为他们的结论提供了适度的信心。

papers.abstract_zh: 在患有儿科自身免疫和自身炎症性风湿性疾病(pedAIIRDs)的儿童中,疫苗接种具有临床重要性但具有挑战性。这些儿童由于其基础的免疫介导性疾病和用于疾病控制的免疫抑制治疗,感染风险增加。同时,免疫抑制可能会降低疫苗诱导的免疫应答,而对疾病复发和活疫苗疫苗安全性的担忧可能导致延迟或不完全的疫苗接种。本论文旨在为接受免疫抑制治疗的pedAIIRDs儿童生成具有临床应用价值的现实世界证据,以评估疫苗接种的安全性、免疫原性和有效性。五项研究涵盖了三种疫苗平台:活疫苗麻疹-麻疹-腮腺炎(MMR)加强针疫苗、新冠-19 mRNA疫苗和重组带状疱疹疫苗(RZV;Shingrix)。在一项针对186名幼年特发性关节炎(JIA)儿童的队列研究中,MMR加强针疫苗与疾病活动性增加无显著关联,包括在使用生物制剂疾病修饰抗风湿药物的儿童中,且未观察到严重的疫苗相关不良事件。对182名JIA儿童的长期评估显示,大多数患者在接种疫苗接种后仍保持对麻疹、麻疹和腮腺炎的保护性抗体。然而,接受生物治疗的患者在接种疫苗接种后五年内对麻疹的血清保护率显著低于未接受生物治疗的患者,支持对血清学监测采取针对性策略。一项系统综述和荟萃分析表明,新冠-19疫苗与儿童多系统炎症综合征(MIS-C)风险显著降低相关。在一项前瞻性队列研究中,针对157名儿科风湿病儿童,新冠-19 mRNA疫苗在几乎所有患者中诱导了体液免疫应答,并在大多数检测患者中诱导了足够的T细胞应答。尽管接受生物治疗的患者抗体浓度较低,但疫苗对出现症状的新冠-19感染的保护效果得以保持。未发现疾病活动性增加、心肌炎或严重不良事件。最后,对十名未感染水痘-带状疱疹病毒(varicella-zoster-virus)的免疫功能低下儿童进行了RZV的非标签使用评估,这些儿童因不适合接种活疫苗水痘疫苗而被纳入研究。在接种两剂后,有九名患者出现了血清学转换。其中两名患者在家庭接触后出现了轻度突破性水痘,但未需要住院治疗或抗病毒药物 治疗。综上所述,这些研究支持从广泛避免疫苗接种向免疫功能低下儿童个体化、针对性疫苗接种策略的转变。研究结果为选择性使用活疫苗、长期针对性监测疫苗诱导的免疫应答、有效使用mRNA疫苗以及进一步评估非活疫苗替代方案提供了证据。这些结果可能有助于未来国家和国际层面针对免疫介导炎症疾病的儿童制定疫苗接种建议。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 疫苗接种 对于儿童自身免疫性和自身炎症性风湿病 (pedAIIRD) 的治疗具有临床意义,但具有挑战性。该研究旨在就 疫苗接种 对接受免疫抑制治疗的 pedAIIRD 儿童的安全性、免疫原性和有效性产生临床适用的真实世界证据。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 五项研究涉及三个 疫苗 平台:减毒活 麻疹-腮腺炎-风疹 (MMR) 加强剂 疫苗、COVID-19 mRNA 疫苗 和重组带状疱疹 疫苗(RZV;Shingrix)。对 186 名幼年特发性关节炎 (JIA) 儿童的 队列研究 进行了 MMR 增强剂 疫苗接种 的评估,并对 157 名儿科风湿病儿童的前瞻性 队列研究 进行了 COVID-19 mRNA 疫苗接种 的研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行了系统回顾和荟萃分析,以评估 COVID-19 疫苗接种 与儿童多系统炎症综合征 (MIS-C) 之间的关联。一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究用于评估患有儿科风湿性疾病的儿童对 mRNA 疫苗 的体液和 T 细胞反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 186 名幼年特发性关节炎 (JIA) 儿童的 队列研究 试验中,MMR 增强剂 疫苗 与疾病活动性增加无关,并且没有观察到与 疫苗 相关的严重不良事件。对 182 名 JIA 儿童的长期评估表明,大多数患者保留了针对 麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹的保护性抗体。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,选定的活体疫苗可以安全地用于患有免疫介导的炎症性疾病的儿童,并且有必要对长期疫苗诱导的免疫进行有针对性的监测。结果还表明,即使接受生物治疗的患者的抗体浓度较低,mRNA 疫苗 在此人群中也是有效的。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可能有助于未来国家和国际 疫苗接种 针对免疫介导的炎症性疾病儿童的建议,支持从广泛的 疫苗 避免转向个体化、治疗 特定的 疫苗接种 策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些证据基于观察性研究和系统评价,可能会受到偏见和混杂因素的影响。然而,这些发现得到了大型 队列研究 和多项研究的支持,为他们的结论提供了适度的信心。

papers.full_text: SummaryThis Research Topic brings together 22 contributions that showcase the breadth of mathematical and computational tools now used to understand and respond to infectious disease threats. Spanning mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analysis, the Research Topic addresses diseases ranging from COVID-19 and influenza to measles, mumps, and dengue. Contributions cluster around three central themes: extracting robust, decision-relevant forecasts from noisy real-time surveillance data; modeling how interventions, mobility, and connectivity shape transmission dynamics; and linking disease burden to environmental, socioeconomic, and health-system determinants. Together, these papers reinforce a unifying message: no single method suffices for every question, and the right analytical approach must be matched to the decision at hand, the data-generating process, and the practical consequences of getting the inference wrong. IntroductionInfectious diseases spread through a complex mix of factors, including pathogens, hosts, behavior, mobility, environment, health systems, and interventions, all of which interact with each other. Mathematical models and data analysis are essential tools for understanding and scientifically simulating these interactions. These approaches enable researchers to draw robust conclusions from incomplete data, formalize competing hypotheses regarding pathogen transmissions and intervention effects, and integrate diverse sources of evidence to generate forecasts and support evidence-based decision-making. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic accelerated the use of these tools on an unprecedented scale, with mathematical models informing decisions regarding lockdowns, vaccine allocations, and healthcare capacity-based planning in near real time. But the pandemic also made clear that good models need clear and evidence-based assumptions, must be tested against real data, should be checked against new data whenever possible, and must be used with an understanding of their uncertainty, not treated as perfect predictions (1–3). The challenge has only grown since: infectious-disease data are increasingly high-dimensional and multimodal, spanning genomic surveillance, mobility traces, wastewater signals, and electronic health records, while the methodological toolkit available to analyze them has expanded just as quickly, from classical compartmental models to machine learning and stochastic optimization.The Research Topic Mathematical Modeling and data analysis in infectious diseases responds to this landscape by bringing together 22 contributions spanning public health, applied mathematics, infectious-disease epidemiology, and microbial sciences. The Research Topic covers a wide range of approaches, such as mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analyses, applied across diseases including COVID-19, influenza, measles, mumps, dengue, and other pathogens of public health concern. Its unifying message is simple: no single method suffices for every question. Instead, the choice of method should follow from the decision at hand, the process generating the data, the observations actually available, and the consequences of incorrect inference or prediction. Robust inference and disease forecastingSeveral contributions in this Research Topic address a central challenge in infectious-disease surveillance: extracting stable, decision-relevant predictions from data that evolve in real time. Rojas-Díaz et al. propose a robust calibration framework for delayed compartmental models, employing controlled parameter initialization and time-varying parameters to fit COVID-19 incidence, intensive-care burden, and effective reproduction numbers across Chilean regions. Their work underscores practical identifiability and numerical stability as prerequisites for translating mechanistic models into tools that can be used operationally in public health decision-making.A complementary forecasting stream combines classical time-series methods with nonlinear learning. Xian et al. demonstrate that a SARIMA–k-nearest-neighbor (SARIMA-KNN) hybrid model improves prediction of acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis in Chongqing, China, relative to its component models and Prophet-based comparators. Cao et al. integrated ARIMA and bidirectional long short-term memory networks through genetic-algorithm weighting, reporting improved COVID-19 forecasts for Japan with external validation in Germany. Alahmadi et al. applied seasonal-trend decomposition together with LightGBM to forecast post-pandemic influenza A in Saudi Arabia, illustrating the value of hybrid approaches when seasonal patterns are disrupted by structural change. Collectively, these studies point to an important direction for surveillance practice: hybrid models can disentangle recurrent linear or seasonal structure from irregular non-linear behavior, but their value depends on prospective evaluation and reporting forecasts alongside calibrated measures of uncertainty (3, 4).The Research Topic also moves beyond single-location time series. One contribution introduces a spatiotemporal graph-learning framework that leverages geographic and origin-destination relationships to capture both contemporaneous neighborhood effects and lagged spatial spillovers in infectious-disease prediction (Liu et al.). Taken together with the forecasting studies above, this work underscores that local incidence is shaped not only by its own history but also by connections to other places, reporting processes, and shifting epidemic regimes. Beyond spatial and temporal structure, several contributions strengthen the statistical foundations needed for infectious-disease data that are non-normal, highly skewed, or operationally heterogeneous. Gharaibeh et al. introduced a two-parameter skewed Loai distribution for positive, right-skewed data and demonstrate its competitive fit to COVID-19 mortality data. At the healthcare-facility scale, Chen and Zhou compared SARIMA, ETS, Prophet, and NNETAR models for forecasting multidrug-resistant organism infection rates, showing that model choice should reflect both forecast accuracy and residual diagnostics rather than point-error measures alone. Disease transmission, interventions, and mobilityMechanistic models offer a principled way to represent intervention timing, human behavior, and disease progression explicitly within the model structure. Babasola et al. formulated a time-delayed model for a potential human outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza, explicitly incorporating incubation, vaccine deployment, vaccine-to-protection delays, vaccine acceptance, residual susceptibility, and compliance with non-pharmaceutical interventions. Their simulations illustrate why early deployment and rapid protection are critical, and why non-pharmaceutical interventions remain especially important before vaccine-induced protection takes effect. Building on this theme, Ntaimo et al. developed an integrated chance-constrained stochastic-programming model for optimal COVID-19 vaccination and intervention strategies across multiple municipalities in Gauteng, South Africa. By incorporating uncertainty in contact patterns, household transmission, age-specific susceptibility and infectivity, and multiple vaccine-effectiveness endpoints, their approach makes risk tolerance an explicit part of allocation decisions. This work exemplifies a valuable bridge between epidemic modeling and operations research: the goal is not merely to simulate an outbreak but also to identify feasible actions under uncertainty.Mobility is another recurring mechanism in this Research Topic. Drawing on cases from 294 Chinese cities, high-speed-rail records, migration data, and socioeconomic covariates, Zhang et al. found that rail connectivity was associated with early intercity dissemination of COVID-19 and that the Wuhan lockdown and transport suspensions disrupted this pathway. The importance of connectivity is echoed in a different setting: an age-structured, stochastic model of measles outbreaks in Northern British Columbia. Irvine et al. showed that inter-community mobility and school-based contact can increase outbreak probability and diminish the effectiveness of interventions, while the combined use of post-exposure prophylaxis and active case finding substantially reduces outbreak risk across scenarios.At a finer spatial scale, Chong et al. combined epidemiological analyses of high-rise residences in Singapore with computational fluid-dynamics simulations, identifying elevated risk within vertical building stacks, and showed how wind direction and cross-ventilation can shape plausible aerosol transport pathways. Together, these contributions demonstrate that interventions must be conditioned on the structure of connectivity itself: rail networks, buildings, households, and social contacts each create distinct transmission pathways that call for correspondingly tailored control measures. Saha et al. extended this perspective across successive COVID-19 waves through a model-based hypothesis-testing framework that compares competing evolutionary explanations while estimating changes in transmission, virulence, vaccination, immunity, and contact patterns. Their analysis reinforces that epidemic trajectories emerge from the coupling of pathogen evolution and human response and that the dominant mechanism driving transmission may shift as population immunity and intervention conditions evolve. Environment, disease burden, and surveillanceA substantial group of papers demonstrates both the value and the interpretive challenges of linking disease surveillance with environmental, socioeconomic, and health-system data. He et al. assessed meteorological influences on influenza incidence in Wuxi, while Yao et al. examined environmental determinants of influenza-like illness across cities in Fujian Province between 2015 and 2023. Tao et al. characterized severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome and its meteorological associations in Jiangsu Province. Extending this line of work, Guo et al. applied generalized additive and distributed lag non-linear models to identify non-linear, interacting, and delayed meteorological associations with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome on China's Jiaodong Peninsula. Hao and Yu take a broader ecological view, using provincial panel models to examine bacillary dysentery in China and link incidence to healthcare capacity, economic development, and forest coverage. Together, these studies show that contextual covariates can strengthen local early warning and risk stratification when lagged, non-linear, and place-specific effects are properly accounted for; they also call for careful interpretation, since ecological and predictive associations do not, on their own, establish causation.The Research Topic also broadens its scope from incidence to population-level burden. Luo et al. used Global Burden of Disease data to quantify trends, geographic inequalities, risk factors, and projected trajectories of childhood infectious encephalitis across Asia. Their results highlight persistent inequities, with lower socio-demographic development associated with higher disease burden, and underscore the continuing need to integrate surveillance, diagnostic capacity, perinatal care, environmental protection, and vaccination.Gong et al. similarly used Global Burden of Disease data, inequality analysis, decomposition, age-period-cohort modeling, and forecasting to characterize the global burden of infectious diseases attributable to drug use. At a more local spatial scale, Hu et al. combined spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatial error models, and Geodetector methods to identify clustered gonorrhea incidence and its interacting sociodemographic, healthcare, and environmental correlates in China. Agrawal et al. synthesized evidence from 47 studies and 61 mumps outbreaks across 21 countries, estimating a pooled attack rate of 14.5% and a pooled complication rate of 10.3%, while documenting substantial heterogeneity by setting, age, and vaccination context. Their meta-analysis underscores the importance of standardized reporting and context-sensitive interpretation in an era of waning immunity and uneven vaccine access. More broadly, burden estimation and evidence synthesis connect model outputs to the equity questions that should guide infectious-disease policy. Spanning mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analysis, the Research Topic addresses diseases ranging from COVID-19 and influenza to measles, mumps, and dengue. Contributions cluster around three central themes: extracting robust, decision-relevant forecasts from noisy real-time surveillance data; modeling how interventions, mobility, and connectivity shape transmission dynamics; and linking disease burden to environmental, socioeconomic, and health-system determinants. Together, these papers reinforce a unifying message: no single method suffices for every question, and the right analytical approach must be matched to the decision at hand, the data-generating process, and the practical consequences of getting the inference wrong. full_text_sections.conclusion: SummaryThis Research Topic brings together 22 contributions that showcase the breadth of mathematical and computational tools now used to understand and respond to infectious disease threats. Spanning mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analysis, the Research Topic addresses diseases ranging from COVID-19 and influenza to measles, mumps, and dengue. Contributions cluster around three central themes: extracting robust, decision-relevant forecasts from noisy real-time surveillance data; modeling how interventions, mobility, and connectivity shape transmission dynamics; and linking disease burden to environmental, socioeconomic, and health-system determinants. Together, these papers reinforce a unifying message: no single method suffices for every question, and the right analytical approach must be matched to the decision at hand, the data-generating process, and the practical consequences of getting the inference wrong.
full_text_sections.other: IntroductionInfectious diseases spread through a complex mix of factors, including pathogens, hosts, behavior, mobility, environment, health systems, and interventions, all of which interact with each other. Mathematical models and data analysis are essential tools for understanding and scientifically simulating these interactions. These approaches enable researchers to draw robust conclusions from incomplete data, formalize competing hypotheses regarding pathogen transmissions and intervention effects, and integrate diverse sources of evidence to generate forecasts and support evidence-based decision-making. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic accelerated the use of these tools on an unprecedented scale, with mathematical models informing decisions regarding lockdowns, vaccine allocations, and healthcare capacity-based planning in near real time. But the pandemic also made clear that good models need clear and evidence-based assumptions, must be tested against real data, should be checked against new data whenever possible, and must be used with an understanding of their uncertainty, not treated as perfect predictions (1–3). The challenge has only grown since: infectious-disease data are increasingly high-dimensional and multimodal, spanning genomic surveillance, mobility traces, wastewater signals, and electronic health records, while the methodological toolkit available to analyze them has expanded just as quickly, from classical compartmental models to machine learning and stochastic optimization.The Research Topic Mathematical Modeling and data analysis in infectious diseases responds to this landscape by bringing together 22 contributions spanning public health, applied mathematics, infectious-disease epidemiology, and microbial sciences. The Research Topic covers a wide range of approaches, such as mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analyses, applied across diseases including COVID-19, influenza, measles, mumps, dengue, and other pathogens of public health concern. Its unifying message is simple: no single method suffices for every question. Instead, the choice of method should follow from the decision at hand, the process generating the data, the observations actually available, and the consequences of incorrect inference or prediction. Robust inference and disease forecastingSeveral contributions in this Research Topic address a central challenge in infectious-disease surveillance: extracting stable, decision-relevant predictions from data that evolve in real time. Rojas-Díaz et al. propose a robust calibration framework for delayed compartmental models, employing controlled parameter initialization and time-varying parameters to fit COVID-19 incidence, intensive-care burden, and effective reproduction numbers across Chilean regions. Their work underscores practical identifiability and numerical stability as prerequisites for translating mechanistic models into tools that can be used operationally in public health decision-making.A complementary forecasting stream combines classical time-series methods with nonlinear learning. Xian et al. demonstrate that a SARIMA–k-nearest-neighbor (SARIMA-KNN) hybrid model improves prediction of acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis in Chongqing, China, relative to its component models and Prophet-based comparators. Cao et al. integrated ARIMA and bidirectional long short-term memory networks through genetic-algorithm weighting, reporting improved COVID-19 forecasts for Japan with external validation in Germany. Alahmadi et al. applied seasonal-trend decomposition together with LightGBM to forecast post-pandemic influenza A in Saudi Arabia, illustrating the value of hybrid approaches when seasonal patterns are disrupted by structural change. Collectively, these studies point to an important direction for surveillance practice: hybrid models can disentangle recurrent linear or seasonal structure from irregular non-linear behavior, but their value depends on prospective evaluation and reporting forecasts alongside calibrated measures of uncertainty (3, 4).The Research Topic also moves beyond single-location time series. One contribution introduces a spatiotemporal graph-learning framework that leverages geographic and origin-destination relationships to capture both contemporaneous neighborhood effects and lagged spatial spillovers in infectious-disease prediction (Liu et al.). Taken together with the forecasting studies above, this work underscores that local incidence is shaped not only by its own history but also by connections to other places, reporting processes, and shifting epidemic regimes. Beyond spatial and temporal structure, several contributions strengthen the statistical foundations needed for infectious-disease data that are non-normal, highly skewed, or operationally heterogeneous. Gharaibeh et al. introduced a two-parameter skewed Loai distribution for positive, right-skewed data and demonstrate its competitive fit to COVID-19 mortality data. At the healthcare-facility scale, Chen and Zhou compared SARIMA, ETS, Prophet, and NNETAR models for forecasting multidrug-resistant organism infection rates, showing that model choice should reflect both forecast accuracy and residual diagnostics rather than point-error measures alone. Disease transmission, interventions, and mobilityMechanistic models offer a principled way to represent intervention timing, human behavior, and disease progression explicitly within the model structure. Babasola et al. formulated a time-delayed model for a potential human outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza, explicitly incorporating incubation, vaccine deployment, vaccine-to-protection delays, vaccine acceptance, residual susceptibility, and compliance with non-pharmaceutical interventions. Their simulations illustrate why early deployment and rapid protection are critical, and why non-pharmaceutical interventions remain especially important before vaccine-induced protection takes effect. Building on this theme, Ntaimo et al. developed an integrated chance-constrained stochastic-programming model for optimal COVID-19 vaccination and intervention strategies across multiple municipalities in Gauteng, South Africa. By incorporating uncertainty in contact patterns, household transmission, age-specific susceptibility and infectivity, and multiple vaccine-effectiveness endpoints, their approach makes risk tolerance an explicit part of allocation decisions. This work exemplifies a valuable bridge between epidemic modeling and operations research: the goal is not merely to simulate an outbreak but also to identify feasible actions under uncertainty.Mobility is another recurring mechanism in this Research Topic. Drawing on cases from 294 Chinese cities, high-speed-rail records, migration data, and socioeconomic covariates, Zhang et al. found that rail connectivity was associated with early intercity dissemination of COVID-19 and that the Wuhan lockdown and transport suspensions disrupted this pathway. The importance of connectivity is echoed in a different setting: an age-structured, stochastic model of measles outbreaks in Northern British Columbia. Irvine et al. showed that inter-community mobility and school-based contact can increase outbreak probability and diminish the effectiveness of interventions, while the combined use of post-exposure prophylaxis and active case finding substantially reduces outbreak risk across scenarios.At a finer spatial scale, Chong et al. combined epidemiological analyses of high-rise residences in Singapore with computational fluid-dynamics simulations, identifying elevated risk within vertical building stacks, and showed how wind direction and cross-ventilation can shape plausible aerosol transport pathways. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the challenge of extracting stable, decision-relevant predictions from real-time infectious-disease data, which is essential for effective public health surveillance and response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The Research Topic includes 22 contributions from public health, applied mathematics, infectious-disease epidemiology, and microbial sciences, covering diseases such as measles, influenza, dengue, and others of public health concern.
analysis.methods: The Research Topic spans mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analysis, with a focus on integrating these methods across diverse diseases and contexts.
analysis.main_results: The studies show that contextual covariates can strengthen local early warning and risk stratification when non-linear and place-specific effects are properly accounted for, and that rail connectivity was associated with early intercity dissemination of COVID-19.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that interventions must be tailored to the structure of connectivity, such as rail networks, buildings, and social contacts, which create distinct transmission pathways. This highlights the need for context-sensitive modeling and analysis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of more accurate surveillance tools and highlight the importance of integrating environmental, socioeconomic, and health-system data to improve public health decision-making.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is moderate, as it is based on a collection of studies rather than a single, focused experiment, and the generalizability of results depends on the specific context and data sources used.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial discusses the growing importance of mathematical modeling and data analysis in infectious disease research, particularly in the context of real-time surveillance and forecasting. The Research Topic includes 22 contributions from various disciplines, addressing diseases such as measles, influenza, and dengue. It highlights the use of diverse methods, including mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, and machine learning, to understand disease transmission dynamics and improve public health responses. The studies show that contextual factors, such as rail connectivity and environmental conditions, play a significant role in disease spread and that interventions must be tailored to specific transmission pathways. These findings emphasize the need for robust statistical foundations and context-sensitive interpretation in infectious disease modeling. However, the evidence is moderate due to the collection nature of the studies and the reliance on diverse data sources, which may affect generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了从实时传染病数据中提取稳定的、与决策相关的预测的挑战,这对于有效的公共卫生 监测 和应对至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究主题包括来自公共卫生、应用数学、传染病 流行病学 和微生物科学的 22 篇贡献,涵盖 麻疹、流感、登革热和其他公共卫生关注的疾病。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究主题涵盖机械建模、统计预测、机器学习、随机优化、计算流体动力学和负担分析,重点是将这些方法整合到不同的疾病和环境中。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究表明,当适当考虑非线性和特定地点的影响时,背景协变量可以加强当地早期预警和风险分层,并且铁路连通性与 COVID-19 的早期城际传播有关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,干预措施必须根据连通性结构进行定制,例如铁路网络、建筑物和社会联系,这些结构创造了独特的 传播 路径。这凸显了对上下文敏感建模和分析的需求。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为开发更准确的 监测 工具提供了信息,并强调了整合环境、社会经济和卫生系统数据以改善公共卫生决策的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据是中等的,因为它是基于一系列研究而不是单一的、集中的实验,并且结果的普遍性取决于所使用的具体背景和数据源。

papers.title: Non-coding RNA-mediated tug-of-war between emerging viruses and host antiviral defense: lessons from animal viruses
papers.abstract: Emerging animal viruses pose persistent threats to livestock breeding and public health, underscoring the need for a deeper understanding of virus-host interactions. Nevertheless, the regulatory roles and conserved mechanisms of host non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) during animal virus infections remain fragmented, and ncRNA-mediated mechanisms for emerging animal viruses are particularly poorly characterized, with no systematic collation or theoretical summarization available. Studies indicate that ncRNAs, including miRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs, have emerged as important regulators of the interplay between animal viruses and their hosts. This review synthesizes evidence from eleven animal viruses covering swine, poultry, ruminant, feline, canine, and mink hosts, with emphasis on virus-induced changes in ncRNA expression and their antiviral or proviral functions. Across diverse virus-host systems, three recurring regulatory paradigms are identified: host antiviral defense, viral hijacking, and viral antagonism. Host cells can dynamically reshape their ncRNA expression to regulate host restriction factors, proviral host factors, and other ncRNAs, thereby influencing innate immune signaling, viral replication cycles, autophagy, apoptosis, and metabolic reprogramming. Conversely, animal viruses, including PEDV, PRRSV, PRV, SVA, AIV, ALV-J, NDV, BVDV, FHV-1, CIV, and MEV, have evolved sophisticated strategies to hijack host ncRNA networks or antagonize ncRNA-mediated antiviral immunity, and remodel the intracellular microenvironment to facilitate viral replication. These paradigms provide a unified theoretical system for understanding and predicting ncRNA-mediated regulatory mechanisms in emerging animal viruses. They also offer references for dissecting the pathogenic patterns of ASFV, SADS-CoV, and future unknown emerging viruses, as well as, for mining, screening, and identifying potential antiviral drug targets.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) in the interaction between emerging animal viruses and host antiviral defenses, with a specific emphasis on measles virus and related entities. The central question is how ncRNAs mediate the dynamic interplay between viruses and host immune responses, particularly in the context of measles virus and its related viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of evidence from eleven animal viruses, including measles virus, covering various hosts such as swine, poultry, ruminant, feline, canine, and mink. The evidence is primarily derived from studies examining virus-induced changes in ncRNA expression and their functions in antiviral or proviral contexts. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or systematic methods for pooling data.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identifies three recurring regulatory paradigms in virus-host interactions: host antiviral defense, viral hijacking, and viral antagonism. These paradigms are presented as a unified theoretical system for understanding ncRNA-mediated regulatory mechanisms in emerging animal viruses, including measles virus.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the regulatory roles and conserved mechanisms of host ncRNAs during animal virus infections remain fragmented, particularly for emerging viruses. There is no systematic collation or theoretical summarization available for ncRNA-mediated mechanisms in measles virus and related entities, highlighting a significant evidence gap.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that the identified paradigms can serve as references for dissecting the pathogenic patterns of measles virus, subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, and future unknown emerging viruses. It also highlights the potential for mining, screening, and identifying antiviral drug targets through the study of ncRNA interactions.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) in the interaction between emerging animal viruses and host antiviral defenses, with a focus on measles virus. It synthesizes evidence from eleven animal viruses, including measles, and identifies three recurring regulatory paradigms: host antiviral defense, viral hijacking, and viral antagonism. These paradigms provide a framework for understanding ncRNA-mediated mechanisms in measles and related viruses. However, the review notes that the regulatory roles of ncRNAs in these interactions remain fragmented, particularly for emerging viruses. The findings suggest potential applications in dissecting the pathogenic patterns of measles virus and in identifying antiviral drug targets.

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出,宿主 ncRNA 在动物病毒感染过程中的调控作用和保守机制仍然支离破碎,特别是对于新出现的病毒。对于 麻疹病毒 和相关实体中 ncRNA 介导的机制,没有系统的整理或理论总结,凸显了显着的证据差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,所确定的范式可以作为剖析 麻疹病毒、亚急性硬化性全脑炎 和未来未知新出现病毒的致病模式的参考。它还强调了通过研究 ncRNA 相互作用来挖掘、筛选和识别 抗病毒药物 药物靶点的潜力。

papers.abstract_zh: 新兴动物病毒对牲畜饲养和公共卫生构成持续威胁,强调需要更深入地了解病毒与 宿主 相互作用。然而,宿主非编码RNA(ncRNA)在动物病毒感染过程中的调控作用和保守机制仍然支离破碎,而新出现的动物病毒的ncRNA介导的机制尤其缺乏表征,没有系统的整理或理论总结。研究表明,ncRNA,包括 miRNA、lncRNA 和 circRNA,已成为动物病毒与其 宿主 之间相互作用的重要调节因子。本综述综合了来自猪、家禽、反刍动物、猫、犬和水貂 宿主 的 11 种动物病毒的证据,重点是病毒诱导的 ncRNA 表达及其 抗病毒药物 或前病毒功能的变化。在不同的病毒-宿主系统中,确定了三种重复出现的监管范式:宿主 抗病毒药物防御、病毒劫持和病毒拮抗。宿主细胞可以动态重塑其ncRNA表达,以调节宿主限制因子、前病毒宿主因子和其他ncRNA,从而影响先天免疫信号、病毒复制周期、自噬、细胞凋亡和代谢重编程。相反,动物病毒,包括PEDV、PRRSV、PRV、SVA、AIV、ALV-J、NDV、BVDV、FHV-1、CIV和MEV,已经进化出复杂的策略来劫持宿主 ncRNA网络或拮抗ncRNA介导的抗病毒药物免疫,并重塑细胞内微环境以促进病毒复制。这些范式为理解和预测新兴动物病毒中 ncRNA 介导的调控机制提供了统一的理论体系。它们还为剖析 ASFV、SADS-CoV 和未来未知新兴病毒的致病模式,以及挖掘、筛选和识别潜在的 抗病毒药物 药物靶点提供参考。

papers.full_text: AbstractImmune dysfunction in hematological malignancies arises from both disease-related alterations and therapeutic interventions, yet comprehensive approaches for characterizing the immune status remain limited. We evaluated an integrated immune profiling strategy combining antigen-specific serology and high-dimensional B-cell phenotyping. Thirty-eight patients with B-cell hematological malignancies receiving ibrutinib-, lenalidomide-, and rituximab-based therapies, or no treatment, were analyzed. Antigen-specific humoral responses were assessed by using a customized protein microarray containing 37 microbial antigens, enabling parallel IgG and IgM profiling. B-cell subpopulations were characterized by spectral flow cytometry. Multiomics factor analysis was applied to integrate serological and cellular data sets and identify major sources of immune variability. Distinct serological and cellular immune profiles were observed across therapeutic groups. Patients receiving ibrutinib displayed lower IgG levels against several microbial antigens and alterations in multiple B-cell compartments, whereas patients receiving lenalidomide-based therapy showed comparatively preserved B-cell populations and broader antigen-specific IgG reactivity. Rituximab-containing regimens were associated with marked reductions in several B-cell subsets. Integrated analysis identified cellular immune features as the major contributors to interpatient heterogeneity, which suggests the presence of treatment-associated immune patterns within the studied cohort. Therefore, integrated serological and cellular profiling provides a scalable framework for characterizing an immune fingerprint with potential prognostic value in patients with B-cell hematological malignancies. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractImmune dysfunction in hematological malignancies arises from both disease-related alterations and therapeutic interventions, yet comprehensive approaches for characterizing the immune status remain limited. We evaluated an integrated immune profiling strategy combining antigen-specific serology and high-dimensional B-cell phenotyping. Thirty-eight patients with B-cell hematological malignancies receiving ibrutinib-, lenalidomide-, and rituximab-based therapies, or no treatment, were analyzed. Antigen-specific humoral responses were assessed by using a customized protein microarray containing 37 microbial antigens, enabling parallel IgG and IgM profiling. B-cell subpopulations were characterized by spectral flow cytometry. Multiomics factor analysis was applied to integrate serological and cellular data sets and identify major sources of immune variability. Distinct serological and cellular immune profiles were observed across therapeutic groups. Patients receiving ibrutinib displayed lower IgG levels against several microbial antigens and alterations in multiple B-cell compartments, whereas patients receiving lenalidomide-based therapy showed comparatively preserved B-cell populations and broader antigen-specific IgG reactivity. Rituximab-containing regimens were associated with marked reductions in several B-cell subsets. Integrated analysis identified cellular immune features as the major contributors to interpatient heterogeneity, which suggests the presence of treatment-associated immune patterns within the studied cohort. Therefore, integrated serological and cellular profiling provides a scalable framework for characterizing an immune fingerprint with potential prognostic value in patients with B-cell hematological malignancies. These findings support further investigation of immune monitoring approaches in larger longitudinal cohorts.Keywords: oncohematological malignancies, integrated immune profiling, immunocompetence, humoral immune dysfunction, cellular immunophenotyping, multiomics factor analysis, treatment-associated immune signatures

full_text_sections.discussion: 5.DiscussionOur study provides an integrated characterization of serological and B-cell immune profiles in patients with B-cell hematological malignancies receiving different therapeutic regimens, including ibrutinib-, lenalidomide-, and rituximab-containing treatments. Distinct serological and cellular immune patterns were observed across the therapeutic groups, highlighting the heterogeneity of immune alterations and immune status of these patients. Since both the underlying disease and treatment can influence humoral and cellular immunity (particularly B-cell subpopulations and antigen-specific antibody responses), a comprehensive assessment of immune status is revealed by an integration of serological profiling with high-dimensional B-cell immunophenotyping.As might be expected, distinct patient subgroups exhibited heterogeneous serological profiles defined by the presence of IgM and IgG antibodies against common mAgs. These serological profiles offer important insights into how serological immunity markers and immune dysregulation may influence disease evolution and infection susceptibility. Understanding pathogen-specific antibody profiles in individuals with reported previous infections may provide valuable information for guiding clinical management of these patients. This has been considered particularly important in infections such as SARS-CoV-2, as it may influence the course of the infection, vaccine efficacy, and hospitalizations. Additionally, it has been demonstrated that some individuals are more prone to reinfection, highlighting the importance of understanding the impact of prior infections and long-lasting antibody responses. Our results reveal how the B-cell compartment is differentially reshaped beyond the antitumoral treatments (ibrutinib-, lenalidomide-, or rituximab-based therapies), because of distinct observed effects on B-cell differentiation, activation, and effector function. Patients receiving lenalidomide-based therapies displayed comparatively higher frequencies of pre–GC B-cells, MBC, and PB subpopulations, together with stronger IgG responses against viruses primarily affecting the respiratory and/or gastrointestinal tracts. These findings are consistent with the immunomodulatory role of lenalidomide, resulting in more effective antigen-dependent B-cell differentiation and comparatively preserved humoral responses. In contrast, Rituximab-based therapies were associated with profound remodeling of the B-cell compartment due to depletion of CD20+ B-cells. Despite this, these patients retained a relatively strong capacity to mount immune responses against multiple mAgs and exhibited a selective increase in IgM reactivity to S. pneumoniae, consistent with the known increased infection risk reported in the literature caused by the depletion of B-cells and the associated impaired humoral immunity. ,− These observations underscore the importance of detailed infection surveillance and tailored preventive strategies in the population undergoing therapy.Ibrutinib-treated patients showed lower IgG responses against several mAgs (including Norovirus, S. pneumoniae, SARS-CoV-2, and Varicella-Zoster virus) together with reduced frequencies of pre-GC B-cells, MBCs, and PBs, suggesting altered B-cell activation and differentiation. These findings are consistent with the known effects of Bruton’s tyrosine kinase inhibition on B-cell receptor signaling and humoral immune responses, ,− as well as the increased risk for opportunistic infections. , In addition, changes in memory B-cell subsets, including reduced frequencies of DN1 (associated with long-lived immune protection) and a relative increase in pro-inflammatory DN2/DN3 populations, may reflect alterations in B-cell homeostasis previously associated with inflammatory and activated immune states. − Collectively, these observations suggest that treatments containing ibrutinib compromise both antibody production and long-term immunity, which may contribute to impaired humoral responses to infections and vaccination. − Overall, the data showed that ibrutinib- and rituximab-containing regimens were associated with reduced frequencies in B-cell subpopulations, whereas lenalidomide-based treatments better preserve the total number of B-cells, highlighting distinct immunological fingerprints associated with each therapy. These effects on cell activation, exhaustion, and isotype switching might present clinical implications for infection risk, vaccine responses, and long-term humoral immunity. Therefore, these therapies can induce profound immune dysregulation through cell depletion, exhaustion, altered tumor microenvironment, and incomplete immune reconstitution. ,− These findings underscore the value of integrative multiomics approaches to disentangle the relative contributions of cellular and humoral immunity to global immune status in oncohematological patients. The predominance of B-cell immunophenotypic features as the principal driver of variance suggested that alterations within the cellular compartment may represent a more sensitive indicator of immune perturbation than humoral immune profiles. While antigen-specific IgM and IgG responses contributed substantially to the integrated model, they explained less heterogeneity, reinforcing that antibody titers alone may not fully capture immune heterogeneity during therapy. From a translational perspective, the strong discriminative performance observedparticularly associated with lenalidomidesuggests distinct therapy-associated immune patterns. Therefore, integrated immune signatures could serve as potential biomarkers of treatment exposure requiring further validation.The integration of serological signatures with B-cell immunophenotypic profiles presents prognostic potential and could provide novel insights into the biology of the diseases; however, our study is limited in several aspects. The cohort was relatively small, predominantly composed of CLL patients, and treatment groups were closely associated with specific disease entities. Furthermore, the lack of age- and sex-matched healthy controls, the cross-sectional study design, the absence of functional immune assays, and the lack of external validation of the ROC analyses limited the transferability of the results. Despite these limitations, the comprehensive serological and immunophenotypic characterization presented here offers valuable insights into immune dysregulation following the treatment. Future longitudinal studies in larger and more diverse cohorts, complemented by functional immune analyses, will be essential to validate these observations, define the dynamics of immune recovery over time, and determine their clinical outcomes. Importantly, to our knowledge, this is the first study to provide an integrated framework combining high-dimensional serological profiling with detailed B-cell immunophenotyping in a clinically relevant cohort of patients with B-cell hematological malignancies. This multidimensional approach establishes a foundation for future biomarker discovery and precision immune monitoring, aimed at improving patient stratification and therapeutic decision-making.
full_text_sections.conclusion: 6.ConclusionsImmune dysfunction is a hallmark of oncohematological diseases, shaped by both the underlying disease and treatments such as ibrutinib- and rituximab-containing regimens. Evaluation of pathogen-specific antibody profiles and B-cell immunophenotypes may provide valuable information for immune monitoring and warrants further investigation in larger prospective cohorts. These approaches could support personalized clinical strategies, including vaccination before immunosuppressive treatment, monitoring pathogen-specific IgM and IgG levels, and considering alternative therapies to mitigate the infectious risk.This study offers an initial immune fingerprint of oncohematological patients across different treatment regimens and highlights the importance of comprehensive immune assessment at diagnosis and prior to therapy. Such an evaluation may enable risk-adapted, personalized treatment decisions and improved monitoring of infections in immunocompromised patients.
full_text_sections.other: 1.IntroductionHematological malignancies comprise a highly heterogeneous group of diseases affecting the blood, bone marrow, and lymphoid organs, which are characterized by widely variable prognoses and a high rate of relapse. They account for 1.2 million new cases worldwide each year, representing about 7% of all newly diagnosed cancers. Lymphoid malignancies, including lymphomas, leukemias, and multiple myeloma (MM), are characterized by clonal proliferation of immune cells and exhibit substantial biological and clinical heterogeneity. Non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHLs) arise from mature lymphocytes at different stages of differentiation and encompass indolent to highly aggressive forms, each requiring distinct therapeutic strategies. Despite major advances in treatment, including targeted therapies and immunotherapies, many patients fail to respond or eventually develop resistance, highlighting an unresolved challenge in disease management. Follicular lymphoma (FL) is a typically slow-growing, indolent B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder arising from follicular center B-cells. It commonly presents with widespread lymphadenopathy, bone marrow involvement, and splenomegaly and less commonly other extranodal sites. FL is the second most common type of NHL, representing about 30%. , Leukemias originate from hematopoietic cells in the bone marrow and lead to the accumulation of abnormal blood cells. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), one of the most common leukemias, is defined by the expansion of CD5+ B-cells and profound immune dysregulation. Malignant B-cells in CLL show resistance to apoptosis and impaired immune activity, resulting in both humoral and cellular immune dysfunction. , Additionally, CLL is also associated with significantly altered T-cell function, which compromises antitumor immunity and increases susceptibility to infections. , Currently, several therapeutic options are available for leukemias and lymphomas, such as chemotherapy, monoclonal antibodies (i.e., rituximab), kinase inhibitors (i.e., ibrutinib), and advanced cellular therapies such as CAR-T cells. , Although these therapeutic approaches have substantially improved patient outcomes, therapeutic resistance remains a major limitation for these pathologies.MM is characterized by clonal expansion of plasma cells in the bone marrow and has benefited from treatments such as proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs like lenalidomide, monoclonal antibodies, and autologous stem cell transplantation. Nevertheless, the disease remains largely incurable, particularly in advanced stages. Increasing evidence indicates that MM therapies are associated with significant immune alterations, leading to an increased risk of infections, including bacterial, viral, and opportunistic infections and reactivation of latent pathogens. , Infections represent a major complication in these onco-hematologic malignancies due to disease-related immune dysregulation and treatment-induced immunosuppression. In CLL patients, viral infections may act as a triggering factor in the early stages of the disease, potentially promoting clonal expansion through chronic antigenic stimulation. Patients with MM, NHL, and FL also show increased susceptibility to infections due to impaired antibody production and T-cell dysfunction, further exacerbated by therapies such as chemotherapy and targeted agents. ,, The infection severity and resolution (with or without sequelae) are influenced by the immune resilience and immunocompetence of the patient, which encompasses mechanisms that restore immune function and maintain self-tolerance. , Immunological memory generated by previous infection or vaccination can mitigate reinfections and reduce severity. − Humoral immunity, mediated by antibodies produced by B-cells, is crucial. B-cells constitute a heterogeneous population of functionally distinct phenotypic subsets well-defined by their maturation status and immunophenotype expression, each contributing differently to antibody production, immune memory, and pathogen neutralization. − In these pathologies, functional B-cells are often depleted or replaced by malignant clones, reducing the ability to sustain effective responses. , Consequently, immune protection and vaccine-induced immunity are highly variable among patients and are influenced by disease stage, tumor burden, and immune impairment. , Currently, the relative impact of several antitumor therapies on humoral and cellular immune responses, particularly in these oncohematological diseases, remains poorly defined and not well understood. Although targeted therapies are designed to reduce secondary effects, these patients often present intrinsic immune dysfunctions. , Immunosuppression is observed with the initiation of the treatment and disease progression due to cumulative therapeutic exposure. , Therefore, early prognosis might be crucial to enable risk-adapted treatment strategies and improve the prevention of infections. Our aim is to characterize antigen-specific humoral responses of patients with oncohematological malignancies undergoing different therapeutic regimens (containing ibrutinib, lenalidomide, or rituximab). For this purpose, serological profiling using a functional antigen microarray was employed to assess their immune response against 37 common microbial antigens (mAgs), and B-cell immunophenotyping was carried out by spectral flow cytometry. By integrating these data sets, we sought to determine how patients receiving different therapeutic regimens differ in humoral and cellular immune profiles, revealing discordance that ultimately shapes pathogen recognition, host defense, disease evolution, and postinfection sequelae. This comprehensive analysis provides insights into immune signatures associated with vaccine responsiveness, recurrent infections, and susceptibility to common pathogens in the population. 2.1.Equipment and SoftwareArrayJet Printer Marathon v1.4, JetSpyder 12 samples, JetStar (ArrayJet, Roslin, UK), Scanner SensoSpot Fluorescence (Miltenyi Imaging GmbH, Radolfzell, Germany), GenePix 4000B Microarray Scanner, GenePix Pro Microarray Analysis Software (Axon, Molecular Devices, San Jose, CA, USA), Orbital shaker (FALC Instruments S.r.l.; Treviglio, Italy), Fisherbrand Microplate Vortex Mixers (Fisherbrand, EEUU), Digital Dry Block Heater (Thermo Scientific, Rockford/IL, USA), 5-laser Aurora spectral cytometer (Cytek Biosciences, CA, USA), R statistics software (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria. http://www.R-project.org/), Infinicyt software (version 2.1.0.a.000; BD Biosciences, San Jose, CA) were used. 3.Experimental Procedures3.1.Clinical Characteristics of the Studied CohortAn oncohematological cohort of 38 patients (Coheńs d ≥ 0.5), aged 51 to 76 years, has been studied. papers.title_original: Integrated Immune Profiling Identifies Treatment-Associated Immune Patterns in Patients with B‐Cell Hematological Malignancies

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate an integrated immune profiling strategy to identify treatment-associated immune patterns in patients with B-cell hematological malignancies, addressing the need to understand how different therapies affect immune responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An integrated analysis was conducted on patients with B-cell hematological malignancies, comparing immune profiles across treatment groups including ibrutinib, lenalidomide-based therapy, rituximab-containing regimens, and no treatment. The study identified cellular immune features as major contributors to interpatient heterogeneity.
analysis.methods: Antigen-specific humoral responses were assessed using a customized protein microarray with 37 microbial antigens for parallel IgG and IgM profiling. Statistical differences between groups were evaluated using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test. B-cell subpopulations were analyzed via PCA and correlation analysis.
analysis.main_results: Patients receiving ibrutinib showed lower IgG levels against several microbial antigens and alterations in multiple B-cell compartments. Lenalidomide-based therapy preserved B-cell populations and showed broader antigen-specific IgG reactivity. Rituximab-containing regimens were associated with marked reductions in several B-cell subsets. The volcano plots revealed differences in IgG profiles across treatment modalities, with significant elevations in IgG against Norovirus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and SARS-CoV-2 antigens in lenalidomide- or rituximab-based treatments compared with ibrutinib.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that treatment-associated differences in immune profiles can be identified, highlighting the potential for immune monitoring to assess infection risk and support preventive strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform immune monitoring approaches in clinical settings, aiding in the assessment of infection risk and the development of preventive strategies for patients undergoing specific therapies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's findings are based on a single cohort and may not be fully generalizable. The evidence is moderate, as the observed heterogeneity in immune profiles was not entirely explained by treatment alone, and the study did not account for all potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated treatment-associated immune patterns in patients with B-cell hematological malignancies using an integrated immune profiling approach. The objective was to evaluate how different therapies, such as ibrutinib, lenalidomide-based therapy, and rituximab-containing regimens, affect immune responses. The methods included antigen-specific serology using a customized protein microarray and B-cell phenotyping via immunophenotyping and PCA. The main results showed that ibrutinib reduced IgG levels against several microbial antigens and altered B-cell compartments, while lenalidomide-based therapy preserved B-cell populations and broadened antigen-specific IgG reactivity. Rituximab regimens led to marked reductions in B-cell subsets. The findings suggest that immune monitoring during treatment could help assess infection risk and guide preventive strategies. However, the study's evidence is moderate due to its focus on a single cohort and the potential influence of confounding factors such as age and sex on immune variability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估综合免疫分析策略,以确定 B 细胞血液恶性肿瘤患者中与 治疗 相关的免疫模式,解决了解不同疗法如何影响 免疫应答 的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 B 细胞血液恶性肿瘤患者进行了综合分析,比较了 治疗 组的免疫特征,包括依鲁替尼、基于来那度胺的治疗、含利妥昔单抗的治疗方案和无 治疗 的治疗方案。该研究确定细胞免疫特征是患者间异质性的主要贡献者。
elements_zh.methods: 使用具有 37 种微生物抗原的定制蛋白质微阵列来评估抗原特异性体液反应,以进行平行 IgG 和 IgM 分析。使用 Wilcoxon 秩和检验评估组间的统计差异。通过 PCA 和相关分析对 B 细胞亚群进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 接受依鲁替尼治疗的患者针对多种微生物抗原的 IgG 水平较低,并且多个 B 细胞区室发生变化。基于来那度胺的疗法保留了 B 细胞群,并显示出更广泛的抗原特异性 IgG 反应性。含利妥昔单抗的治疗方案与几种 B 细胞亚群的显着减少有关。火山图揭示了 治疗 模式中 IgG 谱的差异,与依鲁替尼相比,基于来那度胺或利妥昔单抗的 治疗 中针对诺如病毒、肺炎链球菌和 SARS-CoV-2 抗原的 IgG 显着升高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,可以识别与 治疗 相关的免疫特征差异,凸显了免疫监测评估感染风险和支持预防策略的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为临床环境中的免疫监测方法提供信息,帮助评估感染风险并为接受特定治疗的患者制定预防策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于单个 队列研究,可能无法完全推广。证据是中等的,因为观察到的免疫特征的异质性不能完全用 治疗 单独解释,而且该研究没有考虑所有潜在的混杂因素。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估综合免疫分析策略,以确定 B 细胞血液恶性肿瘤患者中与 治疗 相关的免疫模式,解决了解不同疗法如何影响 免疫应答 的需要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 B 细胞血液恶性肿瘤患者进行了综合分析,比较了 治疗 组的免疫特征,包括依鲁替尼、基于来那度胺的治疗、含利妥昔单抗的治疗方案和无 治疗 的治疗方案。该研究确定细胞免疫特征是患者间异质性的主要贡献者。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用具有 37 种微生物抗原的定制蛋白质微阵列来评估抗原特异性体液反应,以进行平行 IgG 和 IgM 分析。使用 Wilcoxon 秩和检验评估组间的统计差异。通过 PCA 和相关分析对 B 细胞亚群进行分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 接受依鲁替尼治疗的患者针对多种微生物抗原的 IgG 水平较低,并且多个 B 细胞区室发生变化。基于来那度胺的疗法保留了 B 细胞群,并显示出更广泛的抗原特异性 IgG 反应性。含利妥昔单抗的治疗方案与几种 B 细胞亚群的显着减少有关。火山图揭示了 治疗 模式中 IgG 谱的差异,与依鲁替尼相比,基于来那度胺或利妥昔单抗的 治疗 中针对诺如病毒、肺炎链球菌和 SARS-CoV-2 抗原的 IgG 显着升高。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,可以识别与 治疗 相关的免疫特征差异,凸显了免疫监测评估感染风险和支持预防策略的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为临床环境中的免疫监测方法提供信息,帮助评估感染风险并为接受特定治疗的患者制定预防策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于单个 队列研究,可能无法完全推广。证据是中等的,因为观察到的免疫特征的异质性不能完全用 治疗 单独解释,而且该研究没有考虑所有潜在的混杂因素。

papers.full_text: ABSTRACTThe Amapa State, Brazil, in the Amazon region and bordering French Guiana, is a strategic sentinel location for infectious disease surveillance. Ecological pressures such as deforestation, artisanal gold mining, and high human mobility contribute to complex transmission dynamics of arboviruses, bacterial infections, and other pathogens. This study aims to characterize the etiologies of acute febrile illness (AFI) reported in Amapa State in 2018-2020, focusing on arbovirus circulation, bacterial contributions, and emerging pathogens. A retrospective analysis was carried out with 727 AFI cases. Laboratory diagnoses were established using molecular and serological assays, with systematic testing for different pathogens. Definitive diagnoses were obtained in 185 individuals (25.4%), yielding 209 positive results and including 23 cases of co-infection. Dengue virus was the predominant etiological agent (n=109, 52%), followed by leptospirosis (n=20, 9.5%), chikungunya virus (n=16, 7.6%), parvovirus B19 (n=16, 7.6%), measles (n=15, 7.1%), zika virus (n=10, 4.8%), mayaro virus (n=1,0.5%), and other bacterial infections (n=5, 2.4%). Isolated cases of hepatitis A and B, malaria, SARS-CoV-2, enterovirus, and acute Chagas disease were also identified. No hepatitis E virus or oropouche cases were detected. Dengue virus was the leading cause of AFI. Leptospirosis, chikungunya virus, and parvovirus B19 were other prevalent and often underrecognized contributors. The detection of additional viruses highlights Amapa State as a potential zone of “silent expansion” for emerging arboviruses. Co-detection of multiple pathogens underscores diagnostic complexity in regions with overlapping transmission. Strengthening surveillance, expanding laboratory capacity, and prioritizing differential diagnostics are essential to capture epidemiological dynamics and guide public health interventions.KEYWORDS: Dengue, Leptospirosis, Arbovirus infections, Chikungunya fever, Parvovirus B19 MATERIAL AND METHODSStudy design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion.Laboratory proceduresSpecimens were initially processed at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Amapa State (LACEN-AP) following routine diagnostic protocols, including arbovirus screening when clinically indicated. Additional tests, such as serology and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for other pathogens, were performed at the discretion of attending physicians, with results recorded on GAL. Confirmatory local methods included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1 (the latter exclusively for dengue), electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing; for bacterial and fungal infections, ELISA for leptospirosis and blood, urine, and stool cultures were performed; whereas parasitic infections were confirmed using thick blood smears, the Strout test, electrochemiluminescence, and immunochromatographic tests.After initial processing, samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo, Faculty of Medicine, University of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP, LIM-52), in which they were preserved at −80 °C until further testing.Molecular screeningAt LV-IMT-FMUSP, samples underwent real-time PCR assays targeting viral agents. The screening included assays for Pan-Orthoflavivirus and Pan-Alphavirus. The following viral agents were tested: Flaviviruses, Alphaviruses, Orthobunyaviruses: yellow fever 8 , dengue, zika, chikungunya, mayaro, and oropouche viruses 9 .Genus Orthoflavivirus 10 : Japanese encephalitis, Russian spring-summer encephalitis, tick-borne encephalitis, Usutu, West Nile, and Saint Louis encephalitis viruses.Genus Alphavirus 11 : Ross River, O’nyong-nyong, Sindbis, Barmah Forest, Eastern equine encephalitis, Western equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses. Additional real-time PCR assays included pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, such as enterovirus 12 , parvovirus B19 13 , hepatitis E virus (HEV) 14 , and Leptospira spp 15 .GALIn this study, diagnostic test results from LACEN-AP were retrieved via GAL.GAL, the national computerized system, was designed to manage and monitor laboratory routines within the National Public Health Laboratory Network. It is managed by the Ministry of Health via the General Coordination of Public Health Laboratories and tracks the flow of biological samples from collection to final diagnosis, standardizing results and providing real-time data for the surveillance of high-priority and compulsory notification diseases.SINANSINAN, the primary national surveillance database managed by the Brazilian Ministry of Health, is a decentralized system fed by the mandatory notification of diseases and conditions in the National Compulsory Notification List.SINAN provides high-resolution microdata (individual-level records) that include clinical and demographic variables (age, sex, pregnancy status, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations), diagnostic test results, among others.Integration of dataClinical and demographic variables (age, sex, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations) were combined with GAL laboratory results. Using this integrated dataset, data analysis was strictly descriptive, focusing on characterizing the reported cases.For the diagnostic tests either at LACEN or IMT, samples were classified as positive if they were reactive in at least one assay.Statistical analysisContinuous variables are shown as medians and interquartile ranges (IQR), and categorical ones, as frequencies. Subgroup pairwise comparisons were performed via the Pearson’s chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Correlation between monthly cases and NASA POWER precipitation data was assessed using Spearman’s rank test. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate across multiple comparisons. Spatial distribution maps were generated using the geobr, sf, and ggplot2 packages. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, using R(version 4.4.0) via RStudio. Study design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion. RESULTSDemographic and clinical characteristics of the populationThe study population showed a balanced distribution between biological sexes, with a slight predominance of females, accounting for 50.2% (n = 365) of the cases, whereas males represented 49.2% (n = 362). Regarding age, the female sex presented a median age of 28 years (interquartile range : 15-45), with values ranging from0.008 to 90 years. For males, the median age was 26 years (IQR: 12-42), ranging from 0.17 to 88 years. Fever was followed by headache, myalgia, low back pain, nausea, and vomiting. Other manifestations included rash, retro-orbital pain, arthritis, arthralgia, conjunctivitis, and petechiae, with laboratory findings of leukopenia. Chronic comorbidities included systemic arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and chronic kidney disease. Autoimmune diseases and isolated cases of hematological, hepatic, and peptic disorders also occurred.Of the 727 notifications, 585 (80.5%) had arbovirus infection as the initial diagnostic hypothesis—predominantly dengue, followed by chikungunya, zika, and yellow fever. The remaining 142 individuals (19.5%) presented suspicions of other conditions, including Chagas disease, pertussis, COVID-19, diphtheria, Q fever, viral hepatitis, visceral leishmaniasis, leptospirosis, rubella, measles, and toxoplasmosis.LACEN/AP performed 1,239 diagnostic tests, with 195 positive results (15.7%). Dengue was the most frequent diagnosis: 109 cases out of 650 tests (16.8%). Other notable findings included leptospirosis (20/98; 20.4%), chikungunya (16/86; 18.6%), and measles (15/53; 28.3%).Remaining positive cases involved zika (9/62; 14.5%), parvovirus B19 (6/21; 28.6%). Other positive tests for other pathogens were bacterial infections (5/17; 29.4%), Chagas disease (1/80; 1.3%), malaria (2/80; 2.5%), CMV (1/33; 3.0%), hepatitis A (2/24; 8.3%); hepatitis B (1/20; 5.0%), COVID-19 (2/4; 50.0%), influenza virus (1/2; 50%), fungal (1/1; 100%), and arbovirus screening (4/8, 50.0%).At LV-IMTFMUSP, molecular surveillance involved testing 727 individuals by RT-PCR, depending on sample availability. full_text_sections.abstract: ABSTRACTThe Amapa State, Brazil, in the Amazon region and bordering French Guiana, is a strategic sentinel location for infectious disease surveillance. Ecological pressures such as deforestation, artisanal gold mining, and high human mobility contribute to complex transmission dynamics of arboviruses, bacterial infections, and other pathogens. This study aims to characterize the etiologies of acute febrile illness (AFI) reported in Amapa State in 2018-2020, focusing on arbovirus circulation, bacterial contributions, and emerging pathogens. A retrospective analysis was carried out with 727 AFI cases. Laboratory diagnoses were established using molecular and serological assays, with systematic testing for different pathogens. Definitive diagnoses were obtained in 185 individuals (25.4%), yielding 209 positive results and including 23 cases of co-infection. Dengue virus was the predominant etiological agent (n=109, 52%), followed by leptospirosis (n=20, 9.5%), chikungunya virus (n=16, 7.6%), parvovirus B19 (n=16, 7.6%), measles (n=15, 7.1%), zika virus (n=10, 4.8%), mayaro virus (n=1,0.5%), and other bacterial infections (n=5, 2.4%). Isolated cases of hepatitis A and B, malaria, SARS-CoV-2, enterovirus, and acute Chagas disease were also identified. No hepatitis E virus or oropouche cases were detected. Dengue virus was the leading cause of AFI. Leptospirosis, chikungunya virus, and parvovirus B19 were other prevalent and often underrecognized contributors. The detection of additional viruses highlights Amapa State as a potential zone of “silent expansion” for emerging arboviruses. Co-detection of multiple pathogens underscores diagnostic complexity in regions with overlapping transmission. Strengthening surveillance, expanding laboratory capacity, and prioritizing differential diagnostics are essential to capture epidemiological dynamics and guide public health interventions.KEYWORDS: Dengue, Leptospirosis, Arbovirus infections, Chikungunya fever, Parvovirus B19
full_text_sections.methods: MATERIAL AND METHODSStudy design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion.Laboratory proceduresSpecimens were initially processed at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Amapa State (LACEN-AP) following routine diagnostic protocols, including arbovirus screening when clinically indicated. Additional tests, such as serology and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for other pathogens, were performed at the discretion of attending physicians, with results recorded on GAL. Confirmatory local methods included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1 (the latter exclusively for dengue), electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing; for bacterial and fungal infections, ELISA for leptospirosis and blood, urine, and stool cultures were performed; whereas parasitic infections were confirmed using thick blood smears, the Strout test, electrochemiluminescence, and immunochromatographic tests.After initial processing, samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo, Faculty of Medicine, University of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP, LIM-52), in which they were preserved at −80 °C until further testing.Molecular screeningAt LV-IMT-FMUSP, samples underwent real-time PCR assays targeting viral agents. The screening included assays for Pan-Orthoflavivirus and Pan-Alphavirus. The following viral agents were tested: Flaviviruses, Alphaviruses, Orthobunyaviruses: yellow fever 8 , dengue, zika, chikungunya, mayaro, and oropouche viruses 9 .Genus Orthoflavivirus 10 : Japanese encephalitis, Russian spring-summer encephalitis, tick-borne encephalitis, Usutu, West Nile, and Saint Louis encephalitis viruses.Genus Alphavirus 11 : Ross River, O’nyong-nyong, Sindbis, Barmah Forest, Eastern equine encephalitis, Western equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses. Additional real-time PCR assays included pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, such as enterovirus 12 , parvovirus B19 13 , hepatitis E virus (HEV) 14 , and Leptospira spp 15 .GALIn this study, diagnostic test results from LACEN-AP were retrieved via GAL.GAL, the national computerized system, was designed to manage and monitor laboratory routines within the National Public Health Laboratory Network. It is managed by the Ministry of Health via the General Coordination of Public Health Laboratories and tracks the flow of biological samples from collection to final diagnosis, standardizing results and providing real-time data for the surveillance of high-priority and compulsory notification diseases.SINANSINAN, the primary national surveillance database managed by the Brazilian Ministry of Health, is a decentralized system fed by the mandatory notification of diseases and conditions in the National Compulsory Notification List.SINAN provides high-resolution microdata (individual-level records) that include clinical and demographic variables (age, sex, pregnancy status, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations), diagnostic test results, among others.Integration of dataClinical and demographic variables (age, sex, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations) were combined with GAL laboratory results. Using this integrated dataset, data analysis was strictly descriptive, focusing on characterizing the reported cases.For the diagnostic tests either at LACEN or IMT, samples were classified as positive if they were reactive in at least one assay.Statistical analysisContinuous variables are shown as medians and interquartile ranges (IQR), and categorical ones, as frequencies. Subgroup pairwise comparisons were performed via the Pearson’s chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Correlation between monthly cases and NASA POWER precipitation data was assessed using Spearman’s rank test. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate across multiple comparisons. Spatial distribution maps were generated using the geobr, sf, and ggplot2 packages.
